## 140. Selected transport-free `TPacketCGItemUseToItem` fixed-record contract

_Status: selected. `packet.h:605-610` declares `TPacketCGItemUseToItem { BYTE header; TItemPos Cell; TItemPos TargetCell; }`, `HEADER_CG_ITEM_USE_TO_ITEM = 60`, so the record is exactly 7 bytes as two packed 3-byte positions after a one-byte header. `packet_info.cpp:142` registers it and the shared inventory already lists `base_size: 7` and `Registered`, so no framer or inventory change is required. The client mirror at `client/Client/UserInterface/Packet.h:501-505` uses the field names `source_pos` and `target_pos`. This is the only legacy caller that supplies a real destination position to `CHARACTER::UseItem`, so Section 139's reachability analysis is directly reusable. Section 139's server audit already established that `CInputMain::ItemToItem` at `input_main.cpp:1006-1021` is a bare C-style cast with `if (ch)` guards in both the reward and non-reward branches, no length or header check, and no status return, and that the dispatch at `input_main.cpp:3719-3722` is gated on `!ch->IsObserverMode()`. Two read-only source audits are in progress to supply the remaining evidence; the full contract, hazard list, and scope boundary will be appended here before any code is written, and the full locked/offline workspace gate set is required before a completion receipt._



### Section 140 source contract and audit findings

**Wire contract.** `TPacketCGItemUseToItem` is exactly **7 bytes**: header `60` (`0x3c`) at offset 0, the source position at 1..4, and the target position at 4..7. Each `TItemPos` is independently packed 3 bytes, so each position is one opaque `window_type` byte followed by an explicit little-endian `cell: u16`. `packet_info.cpp:142` registers the record, the shared inventory already lists `base_size: 7` and `Registered`, and `resolve_client_frame_size(60)` already yields `ClientFrameSize::Fixed(7)`, so no framer or inventory change is required. Header 60 is **unique within the client-to-game direction**: it is the only `HEADER_CG_*` equal to 60 in either the server or client tree, it is not in `LEGACY_CG_VARIABLE_HEADERS`, and **no `HEADER_GC_*` equals 60** in either tree, so unlike headers 11 and 22 there is no cross-direction numeric collision to guard against. The value 60 is reused only game-to-game and game-to-database, where `HEADER_GD_CREATE_OBJECT` at `server/server/common/tables.h:91` and `HEADER_DG_PARTY_DELETE` at `tables.h:218` both equal it; those are different directions and are not client records.

**The decisive difference from the single-position record.** This is the only inbound record that passes a real target position into `CHARACTER::UseItem`. (The already-receipted `TPacketCGItemMove` also carries a second position, but it reaches `MoveItem`, not `UseItem`, so it is not a counterexample to the narrower and correct claim.) `char.h:1182` declares `UseItem(TItemPos Cell, TItemPos DestCell = NPOS)` and `NPOS` is `(RESERVED_WINDOW, WORD_MAX)` at `length.h:1059`, and `SItemPos::IsValidItemPosition()` rejects `RESERVED_WINDOW` at `length.h:977-978`, so every destination-gated branch in `UseItemEx` is unreachable from header 11. `CInputMain::ItemToItem` at `input_main.cpp:1006-1021` is the only caller that passes a real second position, and the dispatch at `input_main.cpp:3719-3722` gates it on `!ch->IsObserverMode()` while contributing no extra length.

**Destination-gated branch inventory.** `UseItemEx` spans `char_item.cpp:2718-7164` and contains 28 direct `DestCell` references and **21 destination-lookup sites**, all unreachable from header 11 and reachable from header 60: the treasure key at `:3104`; the two Dragon-Soul time-charge cases `USE_TIME_CHARGE_PER` at `:3577` and `USE_TIME_CHARGE_FIX` at `:3633`; the three refine-element cases at `:3668`, `:3721`, and `:3753`; the vnum 71109/72719 pair at `:4868`; the vnum 71051 and 71052 cases at `:5244` and `:5298`; the aura boost at `:5508`; `USE_DETACHMENT` at `:5965`; `USE_RESET_COSTUME_ATTR` at `:6022`; the glove and talisman attribute cases at `:6081` and `:6104`; the five attribute-apply cases at `:6127`, `:6167`, `:6207`, `:6249`, and `:6302`; `ITEM_METIN` at `:6970`; and `ITEM_EXTRACT` at `:7125`.

**Correction to an earlier claim in this section, and the real validator.** An earlier draft of this entry justified the header-11 conclusion by citing `SItemPos::IsValidItemPosition` at `length.h:973-1000`. That is the **wrong function**, and the distinction matters. The unqualified `IsValidItemPosition(DestCell)` inside `UseItemEx` resolves to the member `CHARACTER::IsValidItemPosition` at `char_item.cpp:10010-10049`, and the two functions **disagree**. The member validator accepts `SAFEBOX` at `:10027-10031` and `MALL` at `:10033-10037` when the backing pointers exist, and accepts `ATTR67_ADD` at `:10038-10041` and `SWITCHBOT` at `:10042-10045` behind their build flags, but it has **no** `BELT_INVENTORY` case and so rejects belt positions through `default: return false` at `:10046-10047`; the `SItemPos` member accepts belt and rejects safebox and mall. The header-11 conclusion is unaffected, but for a different reason than first recorded: the member validator returns `false` for `RESERVED_WINDOW` at `:10017-10018`, so the compile-time `NPOS` default is still rejected. The lesson recorded for any later slice is that `IsValidItemPosition` is **ambiguous by name** in this codebase and each call site must be resolved to its defining file before its behaviour is described.

**A guard asymmetry that is safe but easy to misread.** Seventeen of the 21 lookup sites test `IsValidItemPosition(DestCell)` before the lookup. The other four — the treasure key, both time-charge cases, and `ITEM_EXTRACT` — call `GetItem(DestCell)` directly. That is not a hole: `CHARACTER::GetItem` itself calls the member validator first at `char_item.cpp:256-257` and returns `NULL` for an invalid position, so all 21 sites reject the reserved-window default. The safety is real but distributed across two functions, which is worth stating explicitly rather than reading the four call sites as unguarded. One further detail: the treasure-key site at `:3103` calls `GetItem(DestCell)` **twice on a single line**, discarding the first result.

**Twenty-two destination-dependent branches, not twenty-one.** The 21 lookup sites above are the branches that actually dereference the target. There is a twenty-second, `ITEM_HAIR` at `char_item.cpp:2837`, which performs **no validation and no lookup at all**: it passes only the cell word `wDestCell` to `ItemProcess_Hair` at `:9700-9746`, and that helper never reads it. For `ITEM_HAIR` the two records are therefore behaviourally identical and the target bytes are inert, which is worth separating from the other 21 rather than counting as 22 uniform target consumers. Several other destination-independent branches reachable from this header likewise simply ignore the target bytes, including `ITEM_DS` at `:3059` and `ITEM_SPECIAL_DS`.

**Confirmed legacy defects, all above this record boundary.** The audits and direct verification established the following. The vnum 71051 case at `char_item.cpp:5243` validates the **whole** target position and then discards the window byte, calling `GetInventoryItem(wDestCell)` with the cell word alone; `GetInventoryItem` is `char_item.cpp:249-252` and wraps the cell as `TItemPos(INVENTORY, wCell)`, so a valid target in any other window is silently read from the main inventory array. `ItemProcess_Hair(item, wDestCell)` at `:2837` has the same defect. The three refine-element branches validate their target in the ranges `:3667-3700`, `:3720-3742`, and `:3752-3774` and then call `RefineElementInformation(...)` at `:3712`, `:3744`, and `:3776` **discarding its return value** before an unconditional `return true` (an earlier draft of this entry gave `:3724` and `:3755` for the second and third calls; the audit-established values are `:3744` and `:3776`); the helper at `char_item.cpp:10452-10473` accepts only `INVENTORY` cells (`:10454`) and `SendRefineElementPacket` is only sent after those checks, so a valid non-inventory target returns success with no packet, no stored pending state, and no gold spent. `RefineItem` is declared `bool` and both of its results are discarded at `:6003` and `:6012`. The glove and talisman attribute cases switch on `item->GetSubType()` at `:6084-6095` and `:6107-6118` with **no `default:` case**, so an unrecognized subtype reads the target, performs nothing, and falls through to `break` at `:6097`/`:6120`, which exits the item-type switch and reaches the shared `return true` at `:7163` — a silent no-op reported as success. `UseItemEx` mutates the real-time item's sockets at `:2804-2821` and registers a battle-pass mission at `:2823-2825`, and returns `true` for vnum 40004 at `:2827-2831`, all **before** the `switch (item->GetType())` at `:2834` that contains all 21 destination-gated branches; so a request that later fails at a target guard has already mutated the source, and one vnum never consults the target at all. No `Cell == TargetCell` guard exists anywhere in the path, which is why the codec must accept an equal pair. Separately, `CInputMain::ItemToItem` guards `if (ch)` in both the reward and non-reward branches but performs no data, length, or header check and returns no status, and the `ENABLE_REWARD_SYSTEM` branch (defined at `common/prodomodefines.h:200`) pays `REWARD_MISSION_USE_ITEM` on any `true` result, which is how the silent no-op above becomes a reward payout. The `oldCount - 1` log at `:7385` is guarded by `oldCount != item->GetCount()` at `:7383`, so it underflows only if a branch *increased* the count, and it also logs one less than the real count whenever a branch consumed more than one.

**Client findings.** The sole builder is `CPythonNetworkStream::SendItemUseToItemPacket(TItemPos source_pos, TItemPos target_pos)` at `client/Client/UserInterface/PythonNetworkStreamPhaseGameItem.cpp:599-620`, registered as `METH_VARARGS` at `PythonNetworkStreamModule.cpp:2542`. It is the only reference to the record anywhere in the client, and the Python binding at `:798` is its only caller, so there is no second construction path. It assigns all seven bytes (header at `:605`, both positions at `:606-607`) and sends exactly `sizeof(TPacketCGItemUseToItem)` at `:609`, so **every byte is always initialized** on this path — unlike the single-position builder, there is no uninitialized member. The build flag facts behind that are worth stating because they are what make the window byte safe to preserve but unsafe to interpret: the client `EWindows` enum at `GameType.h:295-316` guards `ATTR67_ADD`, `AURA_REFINE`, and `SWITCHBOT` behind `ENABLE_ATTR_6TH_7TH`, `ENABLE_AURA_SYSTEM`, and `ENABLE_SWITCHBOT`, so the numbering of the later entries shifts with the build; in this checkout those three are all defined via `LOCALE_INC.H:7-8,84-85,141` and the server guards the same three at `common/prodomodefines.h:30-31,191`, so the two enums coincide **by configuration, not by construction**. TEA is not applied at send time; the record is copied into a shared send buffer by `CNetworkStream::Send` at `NetStream.cpp:783-790` and encrypted later at flush time in `__SendInternalBuffer` at `NetStream.cpp:204-266`, which confirms this is a plaintext record boundary.

The builder's only pre-send check is `__CanActMainInstance()` at `:601`, which is a player-animation gate defined at `PythonNetworkStreamPhaseGameActor.cpp:28-36` over `CInstanceBase::CanAct()` at `InstanceBase.cpp:1587-1590`. Unlike the header-11 builder at `:561-597`, whose exchange, shop, and attacking checks at `:568-581` are all nested under `__IsEquipItemInSlot(pos)` at `:566`, and unlike the header-13 builder at `:732-776`, which nests twice more at `:741` and `:750`, the header-60 builder has **no `__IsEquipItemInSlot` call, no exchange check, no shop check, and no attacking check at all**. There is therefore no code for a non-equipment source window to bypass; every source/target pair reaches the buffer whenever the animation gate passes.

The Python wrapper `netSendItemUseToItemPacket` at `PythonNetworkStreamModule.cpp:768-800` accepts two arities and has a confirmed defect in each. The 2-argument form at `:774-780` writes only the two cell words through `PyTuple_GetInteger` and leaves both window bytes at the `SItemPos` default, so a window byte of `1` reaches the wire for both positions with no way for the script to see or change it; because both cells are overwritten, the `0xffff` cell sentinel does **not** survive on this path. The 4-argument form at `:781-793` sets both window bytes through `PyTuple_GetByte` and both cells through `PyTuple_GetInteger`. The wrapper **discards the builder's return value** at `:798` and always returns `None` at `:799`, so a full send buffer is unreportable. Three further client defects are confirmed on this path. First, the builder returns `true` at `:601-602` when `__CanActMainInstance()` is false, so "nothing was sent" is reported as success, and `SendSequence()` at `:619` is never overridden by `CPythonNetworkStream` and unconditionally returns `true` at `NetStream.cpp:856-859`, so that line can never report failure either; the only reachable `false` is the `Send` failure at `:611-612`. Second, the Python conversion helpers never check the conversion error: `PyTuple_GetInteger` at `PythonUtils.cpp:127-139` never calls `PyErr_Occurred()`, `PythonUtils.cpp:3` remaps `PyLong_AsLong` to `PyLong_AsLongLong` so the result is narrowed into an `int` with no range check, and the `WORD` and `BYTE` overloads at `:119-125` and `:103-109` narrow unconditionally, so `-1` becomes cell `0xffff`, `65536` becomes cell `0`, and `300` becomes window `44`, each still transmitted with the Python error indicator left set. Those same two overloads read an uninitialized `int val` when the inner call returns early, at `:105-107` and `:121-123`; the `pos >= size` path is unreachable here because the arity switch fixes the arity, but the null-item path is not. Third, the `_DEBUG` trace at `:616` passes two `TItemPos` **structs** to the two `%d` placeholders of `Tracef`, declared as a plain C variadic at `EterBase/Debug.h:15`, and `SItemPos` defines only `==`, `!=`, and `<` at `GameType.h:494-504` with no conversion operator, so that trace is undefined behaviour in exactly the builds where it is compiled (`:615-617`).

Two client facts close out the boundary. The client receive map `CMainPacketHeaderMap` at `PythonNetworkStream.cpp:20-170` is game-to-client only, uses only `HEADER_GC_*` names, and has no entry for 60; no `HEADER_GC_*` constant in the client equals 60, and 59/60 is a gap in that enum's numbering, so the "no cross-direction collision" finding is confirmed. An inbound 60 would therefore be rejected by `CheckPacket` at `:536-543`, which clears the buffer and quits, making the per-phase switch at `PythonNetworkPhaseGame.cpp:197-769` and its `default` at `:766-768` unreachable for this header. And the client's own default-constructed position is `(INVENTORY, 0xffff)` at `GameType.h:426-430`, which is **not** the client's declared `NPOS` of `(RESERVED_WINDOW, WORD_MAX)` at `GameType.h:507` and not the server's `NPOS` at `length.h:959`; so a `0xffff` cell legitimately reaches the wire carrying window byte `1`, and the codec must round-trip it rather than treat it as a sentinel. No source-versus-target comparison exists anywhere on the path, and no missing-`break` fallthrough was found in the arity switch or in the two switches that surround it. One thing could not be established: this worktree contains exactly one Python file, `client/Client/UserInterface/Version.py`, so the gameplay scripts that call `SendItemUseToItemPacket` are absent and any script-side gating is unknown.

**Further confirmed defects, verified against source.** Six more were established and independently checked. First, a **deeper alias in the tuning/detachment path**: `RefineItem` passes only `pkTarget->GetCell()` and `pkItem->GetCell()` into `RefineInformation` at `char_item.cpp:1981`, `:1984`, `:1988`, and `:1993`, dropping both window bytes exactly as the 71051 case does, and `RefineInformation` at `:1865-1913` re-resolves those cells with `GetInventoryItem` before sending the refine dialog and storing the refine source cell. So both the dialog and the stored source can name a different item than the one that was validated. Second, a **buffer-before-reject mutation at six sites**: `:6024-6027`, `:6129-6132`, `:6169-6172`, `:6209-6212`, `:6251-6254`, and `:6304-6307` strip the target's attribute buffs when `IsEquipped()` and only afterwards reject an equipped target. `CBuffOnAttributes::RemoveBuffFromItem` at `buff_on_attributes.cpp:24-31` returns immediately for any cell below `INVENTORY_MAX_NUM` and acts purely on the cell word, so the window byte is irrelevant and a **rejected** request can still remove a worn item's contribution permanently. Third, a **boolean operator error in `CleanSashAttr`** at `char.cpp:10487`: the guard is `(pkTarget->GetType() != ITEM_COSTUME) && (pkTarget->GetSubType() != COSTUME_SASH)` where `||` is plainly intended. The guard therefore rejects only when both hold, so a costume body, weapon, pet, or mount — or a non-costume item whose subtype happens to be `COSTUME_SASH` — passes, and if its `SASH_ABSORBED_SOCKET` is positive the socket and all force attributes are wiped at `:10493-10495`. The same shape does **not** occur in `CleanTransmutation` at `char.cpp:10752`, whose three-way negated conjunction is correct. Fourth, a **single-slot alias**: the `ATTR67_ADD` case at `char_item.cpp:287` returns the one shared `pAttr67AddItem` for every in-range cell, so any in-range target resolves to the same object. Fifth, **opposite equipped requirements inside one branch**: `ITEM_EXTRACT` at `:7124` sends `EXTRACT_DRAGON_SOUL` to `DSManager::PullOut` at `DragonSoul.cpp:515` which requires an **equipped** target, while `EXTRACT_DRAGON_HEART` at `DragonSoul.cpp:413-417` requires a **non-equipped** one; and the Dragon-Soul pull passes `NPOS` at `char_item.cpp:7134`, so `DragonSoul.cpp:500-512` substitutes an auto-chosen slot and **the client's target position is never used for placement**. Sixth, an **asymmetric time-charge result check**: `GiveMoreTime_Per` is guarded by `if (ret > 0)` at `:3594` so a negative return is treated as failure, while `GiveMoreTime_Fix` is guarded by `if (ret)` at `:3642`, so a negative return there still consumes the source and reports success. Neither branch checks `IsExchanging` or `IsEquipped` on the target. Two further scope facts: because 18 of the 22 branches resolve through `GetItem`, a valid target may be `DRAGON_SOUL_INVENTORY`, `ATTR67_ADD`, or `SWITCHBOT` and not only `INVENTORY`/`EQUIPMENT`, and the combined `INVENTORY`/`EQUIPMENT` case at `:262-269` shares one array, so an `EQUIPMENT` window carrying an inventory-range cell returns the **inventory** item. Finally, `ENABLE_DRAGONSOUL_ALCHEMY_PLUS` does **not** gate the two-position time-charge or extraction branches; those are gated by `IsDragonSoul` and `EXTRACT_DRAGON_SOUL` at runtime, so the feature-flag list must not be read as if a Dragon-Soul macro controlled them.

**Scope boundary for the codec.** The codec preserves four raw bytes and writes one fixed header byte. It must not interpret either window byte (the `EWindows` numbering at `length.h:657-676` is feature-dependent), must not require a NUL or decode UTF-8, must not compare or reject equal source and target positions, must not resolve items, windows, or characters, and must not apply ownership, exchange, shop, observer, trade, timing, rate-limit, quest, switchbot, premium, aura, reward, or attribute policy. The 21 destination-gated behaviours above are exactly the logic a future live adapter must reproduce deliberately, because the legacy code reaches them through two different validation paths and, in three cases, not at all.


## 140. Completed transport-free `TPacketCGItemUseToItem` record (2026-09-25 15:31 UTC)

Section 140 is complete. The two-position fixed item-use-to-item record now has a transport-free Rust codec with a source-verified seven-byte layout, malformed-input coverage, locked/offline workspace receipts, and an independent implementation review that was acted on in full.

### Delivered

- New file `protocol/src/cg_item_use_to_item.rs`, 22,901 bytes, 597 lines, SHA-256 `fe02877c398860fa4c655676702e1ddafa26c6656d30c2b02bbb0f3468e352c7`. It publishes `CG_ITEM_USE_TO_ITEM_PAYLOAD_SIZE = 6` and `CG_ITEM_USE_TO_ITEM_WIRE_SIZE = 7`, and re-exports `CG_ITEM_POS_SIZE` from the item-move module. `CgItemUseToItem` carries exactly two `CgItemPos` values as `from` and `to`, and stores **no header field**, because the codec accepts only header 60 and always writes it.
- The codec encodes exactly `[0x3c][from.window_type][from.cell LE][to.window_type][to.cell LE]`, projects a `ClientFrame` with header 60 and exactly six payload bytes, requires the complete seven bytes before reading any field or the header in `decode`, independently requires exactly six payload bytes before the header check in `decode_frame`, and rejects every trailing byte in both representations.
- Both positions reuse the already source-verified `CgItemPos`. A dedicated test pins that the item-move record, the item-use record, and this record place the same packed three-byte position at identical offsets, so the three layouts cannot drift apart later.
- Seven focused tests cover the fixed-size inventory resolution, independent golden bytes for the raw and framed forms, cross-codec offset identity against `CgItemMove`, boundary round-trips for all 256 window bytes crossed with boundary cell words including an equal source/target pair, every raw and framed short and long length crossed with five different header values, every possible header value, and fragmented plus coalesced streaming through the shared `ClientFrameDecoder` alongside a neighbouring `CgShoot` frame.
- The only other change is the single module declaration `pub mod cg_item_use_to_item;` in `protocol/src/lib.rs` (now 20,696 bytes, 683 lines, SHA-256 `701459a1ee48953bf7e4b4dda5998e3c555ac6117e3fe4042fe7e0a24b3ce4f3`). No inventory, framer, compatibility declaration, legacy source, or client source changed, because the shared inventory already listed header 60 with `base_size: 7` and `Registered`.

### Independent review and the four findings it produced

The reviewer `use2item-codec-review140` found no layout, panic-safety, or scope defect, but reported four items and all four were accepted and applied.

1. **A strict-rustdoc gate failure.** The module doc used a redundant explicit intra-doc link at line 9, which `rustdoc::redundant_explicit_links` rejects with `-D warnings`. The reviewer was read-only and derived this from the existing build artifact rather than a fresh run; I confirmed it independently by reading that artifact, which records the exact diagnostic at line 9 column 19, then rewrote the link as a bare reference. The reviewer also correctly explained why the byte-identical text in the sibling item-use module is not flagged: that module has no module-scope `use` of the type, so its label does not resolve on its own.
2. **A false claim in the module doc.** "This is the only inbound record that supplies a real destination position" is wrong, because `TPacketCGItemMove` also carries a second position. The claim was narrowed to "the only inbound record that passes a real destination position into `CHARACTER::UseItem`", with a sentence noting that the item-move record's second position reaches `MoveItem` instead. The same overclaim had propagated into `docs/REWRITE_LEDGER.md`, `AGENTS.md`, and `README.md`, and all four locations were corrected.
3. **A wording inaccuracy.** "Each window byte is an enum" was corrected to "is a `BYTE` field that carries an `EWindows` value whose numbering depends on the build's feature flags", in both the module doc and a test comment, because the legacy field is declared `BYTE window_type` at `length.h:957-959`.
4. **Two test-strength gaps.** The wrong-length cases all carried a correct header and the wrong-header cases all carried a correct length, so a decoder that checked the header before the length would have passed every test. Both paths now cross each wrong length with five different header values. The coalesced streaming path also lacked the drain assertion the fragmented path had, and now asserts it.

Both strengthened tests were then **proven** to bite rather than assumed to: I temporarily inverted the check order in the raw decoder and `every_raw_short_and_long_length_is_rejected_before_the_header` failed, then inverted it in the framed decoder and `every_framed_payload_length_and_header_is_checked` failed. The file was restored byte-for-byte after each mutation and the restoration was asserted.

### Corrections made to this section's own earlier draft

Two errors in the contract text written before the audits reported were found and corrected against source.

- **The wrong validator.** The first draft justified the header-11 reachability conclusion by citing `SItemPos::IsValidItemPosition` at `length.h:973-1000`. The unqualified `IsValidItemPosition(DestCell)` inside `UseItemEx` actually resolves to the member `CHARACTER::IsValidItemPosition` at `char_item.cpp:10010-10049`, and the two functions **disagree**: the member accepts `SAFEBOX` at `:10027-10031` and `MALL` at `:10033-10037` when their backing pointers exist and accepts `ATTR67_ADD` and `SWITCHBOT` behind their build flags, but has no `BELT_INVENTORY` case and so rejects belt positions through `default: return false` at `:10046-10047`, whereas the `SItemPos` member accepts belt and rejects safebox and mall. The header-11 conclusion is unaffected, but it rests on the member validator returning `false` for `RESERVED_WINDOW` at `:10017-1018`. The durable lesson recorded for later slices is that `IsValidItemPosition` is **ambiguous by name** in this codebase, so each call site must be resolved to its defining file before its behaviour is described.
- **Two wrong line numbers.** The first draft gave `:3724` and `:3755` for the second and third discarded `RefineElementInformation` calls; a direct scan of `char_item.cpp` shows `:3712`, `:3744`, and `:3776`.
- **A branch omitted.** The first draft counted 21 destination-dependent branches. There are **22**: `ITEM_HAIR` at `char_item.cpp:2837` performs no validation and no lookup, passing only the cell word `wDestCell` to `ItemProcess_Hair` at `:9700-9746`, which never reads it, so the two records behave identically there. It is recorded separately rather than folded into the count of branches that dereference the target.

### Why this record mattered

This is the only inbound record that passes a real destination into the item-use entry point, and it therefore unlocks **22 destination-dependent branches** that the single-position record can never reach. That makes it the widest single behavioural surface of any record handled so far, and it is why the audit was worth the extra effort. The recorded legacy defects are the two target-window discards at `char_item.cpp:5243` and `:2837`, the deeper `RefineItem` cell-only forwarding at `:1981`/`:1984`/`:1988`/`:1993`, the three discarded `RefineElementInformation` results at `:3712`/`:3744`/`:3776` that report success and still pay a mission reward, the six buff-removal-before-rejection sites where a **rejected** request can still strip a worn item's contribution, the `&&`-for-`||` error at `char.cpp:10487` that can wipe a costume item's socket and force attributes, the missing `default` cases in the glove and talisman subtype switches, the `ATTR67_ADD` single-slot alias at `:287`, the shared `INVENTORY`/`EQUIPMENT` array at `:262-269` that lets an equipment-window target resolve to the inventory item, the opposite equipped requirements inside the single `ITEM_EXTRACT` branch, the asymmetric `if (ret > 0)` versus `if (ret)` result checks in the two time-charge cases, and the client's discarded send result, silent `INVENTORY` defaulting in the two-argument Python form, unchecked narrowing that can turn `-1` into cell `0xffff`, and the `_DEBUG` trace that passes two structs to `%d` placeholders. All of that is source material for a live adapter and none of it is reproduced by the codec.

## 141. Selected transport-free `TPacketCGGiveItem` fixed-record contract

_Status: selected. `packet.h:2320-2326` declares `typedef struct command_give_item { BYTE byHeader; DWORD dwTargetVID; TItemPos ItemPos; BYTE byItemCount; } TPacketCGGiveItem;` with `HEADER_CG_ITEM_GIVE = 83` at `packet.h:66`, inside the `#pragma pack(1)` region at `packet.h:274..3540` and with no build guard around the declaration, so the record is exactly 9 bytes: header at 0, `dwTargetVID` at 1..5, the packed 3-byte `ItemPos` at 5..8, and `byItemCount` at 8. `packet_info.cpp:161` registers it and the shared inventory already lists `base_size: 9` and `Registered`, so no framer or inventory change is required. This boundary completes the core inbound item lifecycle alongside the already-receipted item-move, item-use, and item-use-to-item records, and it is the first fixed inbound CG record to carry a `u32` character identifier and a `u8` count, so it exercises field kinds the earlier slices did not.

Four facts already established by direct inspection, each to be confirmed or corrected by the audits. First, `byItemCount` is declared on the wire and **read nowhere**: the only occurrence in the whole server tree is the declaration itself at `packet.h:2325`, and `input_main.cpp` never references it, so a byte is transmitted and then discarded. Second, **header 83 collides across directions**: `HEADER_CG_ITEM_GIVE = 83` at `packet.h:66` and `HEADER_GC_PARTY_PARAMETER = 83` at `packet.h` share the value, and the colliding game-to-client record `TPacketGCPartyParameter` at `packet.h:2010-2014` is only **2 bytes** (`BYTE bHeader; BYTE bDistributeMode;`), so the same number means a 9-byte inbound request and a 2-byte outbound record; no header table may be shared across directions. Third, the client **renames** the constant to `HEADER_CG_GIVE_ITEM` at `client/Client/UserInterface/Packet.h` while the server calls it `HEADER_CG_ITEM_GIVE`, although the client struct at `client/Client/UserInterface/Packet.h:911-917` is byte-identical to the server's. Fourth, the client's sole builder `CPythonNetworkStream::SendGiveItemPacket` at `client/Client/UserInterface/PythonNetworkStreamPhaseGame.cpp:4378-4390` has **no `__CanActMainInstance()` gate at all**, unlike every other item builder audited so far, and narrows a signed `int iItemCount` into the `BYTE byItemCount` field with no range check, while the Python wrapper `netSendGiveItemPacket` at `client/Client/UserInterface/PythonNetworkStreamModule.cpp:938-970` has a `default: break;` at `:963-964` rather than an early return, so **a wrong argument count falls through and sends uninitialized stack values for the target identifier, the cell, and the count**.

The server handler is `CInputMain::ItemGive` at `input_main.cpp:3174-3183`: a bare C-style cast, `CHARACTER_MANAGER::instance().Find(p->dwTargetVID)`, and either `ch->GiveItem(to_ch, p->ItemPos)` or a fixed chat string, with no length, header, or data check, no status return, and no use of `byItemCount`. The dispatch at `input_main.cpp:3723-3726` gates only on `!ch->IsObserverMode()`. Two read-only source audits are in progress to supply the remaining evidence for the full contract, hazard list, and scope boundary; the ledger will be extended before any code is written, and the complete locked/offline workspace gate set is required before a completion receipt.

The size of the wrapper defect class was measured twice and **both early measurements were wrong**, so the corrected figure is recorded here. The first scan used a function-end detector that did not account for this file's CRLF line endings, so every function body ran to the end of the file and the scan reported 102 affected wrappers. The second scan mis-paired wrapper names with a file-wide list of scalar declarations and reported 51. Both were discarded. A re-scan with a CRLF-aware end-of-function detector, validated first against two known functions (`netSendGiveItemPacket` and `netSendItemUseToItemPacket`, each correctly spanning 32 lines, matching `:938-970` and `:768-800` respectively), gives the real answer: of the **173** wrappers in `PythonNetworkStreamModule.cpp`, exactly **2** have a `default: break;` that falls through to a send. Both also pass an uninitialized scalar onto the wire, and there is no third case.

- `netSendGiveItemPacket` at `PythonNetworkStreamModule.cpp:938-970`, confirmed above, leaks uninitialized `int iTargetVID` and `int iItemCount` into `dwTargetVID` and `byItemCount`. The `TItemPos Cell` local at `:941` is *not* garbage, because `SItemPos` supplies a default constructor, so it becomes `(INVENTORY, 0xffff)`.
- `netSendSafeboxCheckoutPacket` at `PythonNetworkStreamModule.cpp:1355-1383` has the same shape: `int iSafeBoxPos;` at `:1357`, a `default: break;` at `:1376-1377`, and an unguarded `rns.SendSafeBoxCheckoutPacket(iSafeBoxPos, InventoryPos)` at `:1381`. Its `TItemPos InventoryPos` at `:1358` is default-constructed to `(INVENTORY, 0xffff)`, so the only genuinely uninitialized value is the safebox position. This one belongs to the header-77 safebox-checkout boundary rather than to this section, and is noted here so it is not rediscovered as if it were new.

The remaining 171 wrappers either validate arity with an early return or are getters that do not write to a packet. The general lesson is recorded for later client audits: `default: break;` in this file is rare, so its presence is a real signal and not a house style, and a claim about how many wrappers share a defect must be measured with a delimiter that has been validated against a known case before the number is repeated.


### Section 141 server-side audit: independently verified findings

The read-only server audit `give-server-audit141` was checked line by line against the source before anything below was recorded. Every claim that mattered was re-read directly; the ones that did not survive verification are noted as rejected rather than silently dropped.

**Correction applied to this section's own codec docs.** The first draft of the module scope sentence said the legacy path performs "the lookup, ownership, distance, and transfer policy". That is wrong about ownership. There is **no ownership check and no same-map check anywhere** on the header-83 path. The only locality test is a two-dimensional distance comparison at `char_item.cpp:9259-9260`, `DISTANCE_APPROX(GetX() - from->GetX(), GetY() - from->GetY()) > 2000`. No `GetMapIndex()` comparison exists on this path at all. The module doc now says so explicitly, so a future adapter does not assume either check exists. The audit correctly declined to claim a reachable cross-map give, because whether one game-server process hosts more than one map index cannot be established from this worktree; that limit is preserved.

**Verified structure.** `CHARACTER::GiveItem` is declared at `char.h:1204` and defined at `char_item.cpp:9226-9251`. Its entire body is five checks: `CanHandleItem()` at `:9228`, a quest-script-running check at `:9232`, `GetItem(Cell)` at `:9239`, an `IsExchanging()` lock at `:9241`, and `victim->CanReceiveItem(this, item)` at `:9243`, after which `ReceiveItem` runs and `true` is returned unconditionally at `:9246`. `CanReceiveItem` at `char_item.cpp:9253-9421` opens with `if (IsPC()) return false;` at `:9255-9256`, so **the receiver can never be a player**: this record is a give-to-NPC record, not a player-to-player transfer. Its per-race switch covers the blacksmith, alchemist, fisherman, campfire, stable, and desert horse trainers, and every other NPC, including all quest NPCs, falls through to `return true` at `:9416-9418`. `ReceiveItem` at `char_item.cpp:9423-9517` returns `void`, which is the root of defect D1 below.

**Verified defects, each re-read at the cited lines.**

- **D1, a discarded success signal.** `ReceiveItem` is `void`, `GiveItem` returns `true` at `:9246` regardless of whether anything moved, and `CInputMain::ItemGive` at `input_main.cpp:3178` discards even that boolean. The client therefore cannot distinguish a real transfer from a no-op, and neither outcome reaches the client. Concrete no-op-but-true cases: a stable trainer given a vnum that is not one of the six horse items; a `BLACKSMITH_*` NPC, which only opens the refine UI and moves nothing; the Meley statue when the map test fails.
- **D2, a consumed item for a refused action.** `from->ReviveHorse()` at `char_item.cpp:9496` returns `bool` and its result is **discarded**, then `item->SetCount(item->GetCount()-1)` at `:9497` runs anyway, and `[LS;452]` is sent at `:9498`. `CHorseRider::ReviveHorse` returns `false` when `GetHorseLevel() <= 0` or `GetHorseHealth() > 0`, so the item is lost, the player is told it worked, and the horse is not revived.
- **D3, the same shape, worse.** `from->FeedHorse()` at `:9504` is `void` and silently does nothing when `GetHorseLevel() <= 0 || GetHorseHealth() <= 0`, yet `:9505` sends `[LS;453]`, `:9506` decrements the stack, and `:9507` fires `SE_HPUP_RED`. The player pays, is told it worked, and sees a health effect for a horse that was not fed.
- **D4, an out-of-bounds read on a reachable-looking path.** `MeleyLair.cpp:1311` reads `CMgrMap* pMap = m_RegGuilds.find(pkGuild->GetID())->second;` with **no `end()` test**, and the guard on the next line, `if (!pMap)`, is therefore dead code, because `->second` on `end()` is already undefined behaviour. `m_RegGuilds` is a `std::map<DWORD, CMgrMap*>` declared at `MeleyLair.h:134` and is cleared at `MeleyLair.cpp:955` and `:971`, so the key can genuinely be absent. The same unchecked pattern recurs at `:1267`, `:1277`, and `:1296`, none of which is on the give path.
- **D5, the position window is structurally discarded.** The call sites at `char_item.cpp:9458` and `:9475` pass `item->GetCell()`, a bare cell word, into `RefineInformation`, whose live signature under the active `ENABLE_CUSTOM_INVENTORY` flag (`prodomodefines.h:202`) is `RefineInformation(WORD bCell, BYTE bType, int iAdditionalCell)` at `:1865`. The window the client sent, and the window the item actually lived in, are both gone, and `:1876` re-resolves the item as `GetInventoryItem(bCell)`, that is `GetItem(TItemPos(INVENTORY, bCell))`. For a `DRAGON_SOUL_INVENTORY`, `ATTR67_ADD`, or `SWITCHBOT` source the re-resolution either fails the bound at `:1867-1868` or resolves an unrelated inventory item, and `GiveItem` still returns `true`. Worth recording separately: the **inactive** `#else` branch at `:1870-1873` uses `bCell > INVENTORY_MAX_NUM` where the live branch correctly uses `>=`, so that off-by-one is real but dead; it must not be "fixed" in place.
- **D6, a bypass of the protected-inventory lock.** `char_item.cpp:9228` calls `CanHandleItem()` with no `IsSecured()` test, although the `__ENABLE_INVENTORY_PROTECTED_SYSTEM__` guard is present at all five sibling item paths: `DropItem` `:7489`, `DestroyItem` `:7429`, `UseItemEx` `:7716`, `CanEquipNow` `:10183`, and `CanUnequpNow` `:10212`. The flag is active at `prodomodefines.h:169`, so header 83 is a real way around a lock that five other records respect.
- **D7, state mutated before validation with no rollback.** `from->SetQuestNPCID(GetVID())` at `:9436` and `:9513` runs before `TakeItem` can fail, and `m_dwQuestNPCVID` at `char.h:1789` is cleared only by quest-Lua paths, on the NPC rather than the player, or by the Meley manager. `CHARACTER::GetQuestNPC()` at `char.cpp:7615-7618` resolves the stale value through a reused VID map, so a failed hand-in can leave a player pointing at a reused identifier. Recorded as a stale-identifier hazard rather than a confirmed crash.
- **D8, an equipped item can be handed over.** `:9241` tests only `!item->IsExchanging()`, while the sibling item paths test `IsExchanging() || IsEquipped()` at `:3106`, `:3670`, `:4870`, `:5256`, and `:5967`. Equipment cells pass both of this path's gates, so an equipped item can be destroyed by a quest NPC without ever passing `CanUnequpNow`. This is a policy bypass and not a leak, because `RemoveFromCharacter` unequips first at `item.cpp:369-377`.
- **D9, an undefended handler.** `input_main.cpp:3176` is a bare C-style cast of `c_pData` with no in-handler length, header, or alignment check. The nine-byte guarantee comes only from the framing layer at `input.cpp:83` and `:92-93` plus the registration at `packet_info.cpp:161`, which the audit correctly confirmed does hold. The `DWORD` at offset 1 is never four-byte aligned, which is harmless on the x86 build and a latent portability fault. This is the same defect class already recorded for `input_login.cpp:265-304` and `:454-515`.

**Accepted as a hazard, explicitly not as a defect.** `char_item.cpp:9497` and `:9506` compute `item->GetCount()-1` on a `DWORD`. A count of zero would wrap to `0xFFFFFFFF` and then be clamped **up** to `g_bItemCountLimit` by `CItem::SetCount` instead of removing the item. The audit searched for a producer and found none: `ITEM_MANAGER::CreateItem` clamps stackables to at least 1 at `item_manager.cpp:256`, and `SetCount(0)` on an owned item destroys it at `item.cpp:307-341`. The claim is therefore recorded as unreachable-unproven rather than asserted.

**Checked and cleared, so it is not re-litigated later.** `GetPCForce()` at `questmanager.cpp:1073-1085` never returns `NULL`, so `:9232` is not a null dereference. `GetItem`'s `ATTR67_ADD` branch at `:279-288` returns one unindexed pointer, and `ATTR67_ADD_SLOT_MAX` is 1 at `length.h:202`, so only cell 0 passes and the code is correct. `fishing::Grill` copies the count at `fishing.cpp:843` before `SetCount(0)` destroys the item at `:846`, so there is no use-after-free. The two disagreeing validity predicates are real but not a hole, because `GetItem` returns `NULL` for `SAFEBOX` and `MALL` at `:301-302` even though `CHARACTER::IsValidItemPosition` accepts them at `:10027-10037`.


**Cross-direction reuse of 83, verified exhaustively.** Reading the full server header enum at `packet.h:19-272` yields exactly two hits for the value 83: `HEADER_CG_ITEM_GIVE` at `:66` and `HEADER_GC_PARTY_PARAMETER` at `:170`. The colliding outbound record is the two-byte `TPacketGCPartyParameter` at `packet.h:2010-2014`, so the collision is a 2-byte-versus-9-byte mismatch **inside the same enum block**. I re-ran the search myself and reproduced both lines; my first attempt returned an empty list only because the search pattern was anchored to the start of the line while the constant is indented by a tab, which is a bug in my own check rather than a difference in the source. The client tree has exactly the same two values at `Packet.h:63` and `:167`. The game-to-database and game-to-game directions contain no 83 in any build configuration, and 83 does not appear in any variable-length client-to-game list, so the eight payload bytes are the record and nothing follows it. Both the dead-phase analyzer `CInputDead::Analyze` at `input_main.cpp:4088-4130` and the peer analyzer handle no 83, so a dead player or a peer sending header 83 does nothing. Conclusion recorded: no header table may ever be shared between the client-to-game and game-to-client directions.

**Layout is build-independent, confirmed mechanically rather than inferred.** `packet.h:274` opens `#pragma pack(1)` and `:3540` closes it, and `TPacketCGGiveItem` at `:2320-2326` sits inside that span with **zero** preprocessor conditionals around it, nor around the header constant at `:66` (unlike `HEADER_CG_ITEM_SELL` at `:31-33`, which is behind `ENABLE_SELL_ITEM`). In the client, `length.h:956` opens `#pragma pack(push, 1)` and `:1274` closes it; `TItemPos` at `:957-1057` has conditionals only at `:988-991`, `:992-995`, `:1022-1027`, and `:1028-1044`, and every one of those is inside a member function, never around the two data members `BYTE window_type; WORD cell;` at `:959-960`. So the record is exactly nine bytes under every combination of the build flags, which is a stronger statement than "it happens to be nine today".

**Feature dependence is meaning-only, and it is why the window byte must stay opaque.** `__AURA_SYSTEM__` (`prodomodefines.h:30`), `__ATTR_6TH_7TH__` (`:31`), and `ENABLE_SWITCHBOT` (`:191`) each **insert a member into the `EWindows` enumeration** at `length.h:665-673`, which shifts `SWITCHBOT`, `BELT_INVENTORY`, and `GROUND` to different numbers depending on the build. That is the strongest available justification for never interpreting the window byte. `ENABLE_CUSTOM_INVENTORY` (`:202`) selects `INVENTORY_AND_EQUIP_SLOT_MAX` at `length.h:925-927` and selects the `RefineInformation(WORD, ...)` overload, which is what makes defect D5 above possible. `__SASH_SYSTEM__`, `__CHANGELOOK_SYSTEM__`, `__MELEY_LAIR_DUNGEON__`, and `__ENABLE_INVENTORY_PROTECTED_SYSTEM__` only add a check branch. None of them adds, removes, or reorders a field.

**The dead field is confirmed dead, with the whole consumer set enumerated.** `TPacketCGGiveItem` appears in the entire repository at only six places: its definition and closing brace at `packet.h:2320` and `:2326`, the registration at `packet_info.cpp:161`, the single bare cast at `input_main.cpp:3176`, the client's identical definition at `client/Client/UserInterface/Packet.h:911` and `:917`, and the client's builder at `PythonNetworkStreamPhaseGame.cpp:4380`. `byItemCount` appears in the whole server tree only at its own declaration `packet.h:2325`. The other server hits, at `shop_manager.cpp:715`, `:794`, `:810`, and `common/tables.h:825`, are the unrelated `SShopTable::byItemCount` field of a boot-time shop table defined at `tables.h:820-830`, in a different struct and a different direction; it is not a reader of this nine-byte layout. The sole writer of the byte is the client, at `PythonNetworkStreamPhaseGame.cpp:4378-4390`, which assigns an unchecked `int` into it. So the byte is genuinely dead on the wire contract, and the codec must still round-trip it because it is physically present in every frame.

**Scope boundary, recorded as a checklist.** Framing and the size lookup stay outside, as do TEA and descriptor buffering, phase dispatch and the observer gate, `CHARACTER_MANAGER::Find` and its own sanity check, all eight `CanHandleItem` state checks, the quest-running probe, position validity and window range policy, `IsExchanging`, the `IsPC` rejection, the 2-D distance limit, the entire per-race receiver switch, and every item mutation including `ITEM_MANAGER::RemoveItem`, `CItem::SetCount`, and `CItem::RemoveFromCharacter`. Defects D1 through D10 stay documented as legacy defects and are not to be "fixed" inside the codec. The client's unchecked `int`-to-`BYTE` narrowing of the count is precisely why every byte value is a legitimate wire value.

**Two items the audit explicitly refused to claim, preserved here as unproven.** First, whether one game-server process can host characters of more than one map index cannot be established from this worktree, so the missing same-map check is recorded as an absent check and **not** as a reachable cross-map give. Second, the quest Lua scripts that decide how many units a quest `TakeItem` consumes are data and are absent from this worktree, so "every quest handler removes the whole stack" is unproven even though the `item.remove()` binding at `questlua_item.cpp:91-105` is confirmed to remove a whole item.


### Section 141 independent implementation review: two real test defects and two false documentation claims

The reviewer `give-codec-review141` worked read-only and, unusually well, built a throwaway crate under `/tmp` holding verbatim copies of the sibling modules and the new one, with the workspace lint table reproduced, so it could run the real gates and thirteen mutations without touching the repository. Its verdict on the wire codec itself was that the layout is byte-exact, that no byte legacy permits is rejected, that the decode order is correct, that storing no header is right, that there is no panic, unsafe, or overflow risk, that no gameplay policy leaks in, and that the format, strict lint, and documentation gates all pass. All four of its substantive findings were accepted and fixed, and both test defects were **reproduced locally before being fixed**.

**Two documentation claims in the new codec were false and are corrected.** The module doc said the record is "the fourth legacy record to carry that packed three-byte position". That is wrong about the legacy source. `packet.h` embeds a packed `TItemPos` in **twelve** `TPacketCG*` records, and by my own count this one is the twelfth in declaration order, not the fourth: `TPacketCGItemUse` `:599`, `TPacketCGItemUseToItem` `:605`, `TPacketCGItemDrop` `:612`, `TPacketCGItemDrop2` `:619`, `TPacketCGItemDestroy` `:627`, `TPacketCGItemMove` `:633`, `TPacketCGItemSell` `:650`, `TPacketCGExchange` `:724`, `TPacketCGPrivateShopItemCheckin` `:1380`, `TPacketCGSafeboxCheckout` `:1979`, `TPacketCGSafeboxCheckin` `:1990`, and `TPacketCGGiveItem` `:2320`. The claim is now scoped to what is actually true: this is the fourth **Rust codec** to reuse the shared `CgItemPos`, and the legacy count of twelve is stated alongside it. The same overstatement appeared in a test comment, which additionally mixed two offset spaces by claiming the position "starts at 0" while the very next lines index `[1..4]`; zero is the framed-payload offset, and on the wire the position starts at 1. Both are fixed.

**Defect 8-1, reproduced locally: the framed header check was untested.** Deleting `check_header(frame.header)?` from `decode_frame` left **all eight tests green**. The cause is that every framed case paired a wrong header with a wrong length, so the length branch always won, and the exhaustive 0..=255 header sweep only exercised the raw path. The consequence is that `CgItemGiveError::InvalidHeader` was **unreachable from `decode_frame` in the entire suite**, and the corresponding `Display` arm was only reached by hand-built values. The framed test now sweeps every header value at the correct payload length and asserts that header 0x53 at that length is accepted. Re-running the same mutation after the fix makes the test fail, so the assertion now bites.

**Defect 8-2, reproduced locally: the streaming test did not prove what it claimed.** Replacing the byte-at-a-time feed with a single bulk `feed` left **all eight tests green**. The comment promised to prove the decoder retains a partial tail, but nothing ever observed `try_decode()` returning `None` mid-record. The sibling `cg_item_move.rs` and `cg_shoot.rs` do assert that intermediate `None`, which is the assertion that bites. The test now feeds one byte at a time, asserts `try_decode()` yields nothing, that `buffered_len()` equals the number of bytes fed, and that `peek_header()` is stable at every boundary from 1 to 8 bytes. Re-running the same mutation after the fix makes the test fail.

While fixing 8-2 I introduced a real bug of my own and caught it by running the test rather than by reading it: the loop fed the cumulative prefix `wire[..n]` on every iteration, so the buffer grew quadratically and the `buffered_len() == n` assertion failed with 3 against 2. The loop now feeds only the newly arrived slice, and the final assertion was corrected to the total buffered length, since the decoder already holds the earlier bytes.

**Three lesser findings accepted.** A dead `bytes.clear()` and a vestigial `mut` were removed. The bulk half of the streaming test now asserts the middle frame's header instead of discarding it, and the feeds are `unwrap`ed rather than silently dropping a possible allocation error. A gap was closed by adding correct-header-with-wrong-length cases, which the suite previously lacked entirely.

**Documentation gap closed.** The "legacy facts kept out of the codec" list recorded the harmless count narrowing but omitted the two sharpest client defects and the server's bare cast. It now names the ungated builder, the `default: break;` that sends uninitialized stack values, the server-side bare C-style cast, and the observer-only dispatch gate, matching the explicit defect notes the three sibling item modules already carry.

**Ledger line range corrected.** The two-byte `TPacketGCPartyParameter` occupies `packet.h:2010-2014`, not `2010-2013`; the closing line had been dropped. The reviewer also noted that the project documentation still described only the earlier item modules, which was true and has since been fixed in `AGENTS.md` and `README.md`, including a stale "21 destination-gated branches" figure in the `AGENTS.md` item-use-to-item rule that is now 22 with the inert `ITEM_HAIR` branch named.


### Section 141 client-side audit: independently verified findings

The read-only client audit `give-client-audit141` was checked against the source before anything below was recorded.

**The builder is genuinely ungated, and that is a structural difference, not an oversight.** `CPythonNetworkStream::SendGiveItemPacket` at `PythonNetworkStreamPhaseGame.cpp:4378-4390` assigns all nine bytes and sends, with **no** `__CanActMainInstance()` call, no cell-legality check, and no `Tracef` on the failure branch. The already-audited siblings all gate: `SendItemUsePacket` at `PythonNetworkStreamPhaseGameItem.cpp:563-564`, `SendItemUseToItemPacket` at `:601-602`, and `SendItemMovePacket` at `:734-735`, and the two of them that move items additionally check trade, shop, and attacking state. The gate itself is `PythonNetworkStreamPhaseGameActor.cpp:28-36`. The immediate neighbour `SendFishingPacket` at `:4366-4376` is also ungated, so the omission is not an artifact of the file's tail. Consequence: a script can emit this transfer while the character is dead, loading, trading, shopping, or attacking, and the only thing that can stop the record is a full send buffer. The audit confirmed by exhaustive search that the only caller is the Python wrapper: five hits for `SendGiveItemPacket` across the client tree, all of them the declaration, the definition, the wrapper, its call, and the method table.

**The wrapper can put uninitialized stack memory on the wire, and the exact byte count is now recorded.** `netSendGiveItemPacket` at `PythonNetworkStreamModule.cpp:938-970` handles only arities 3 and 4, and its `default: break;` at `:963-964` falls straight through to the send at `:968`. On any other arity, five of the nine bytes are stack garbage: `dwTargetVID` at 1..5 and the count byte at 8 come from uninitialized `int` locals declared at `:940` and `:942`. The other four bytes are deterministic: the header 0x53 from the constant, `window_type` 1 and `cell` 0xffff from the `SItemPos()` default constructor at `GameType.h:426-430`, because `TItemPos Cell;` at `:941` is default-constructed rather than left indeterminate. The record is still fully assembled and still sent, because the builder has no validation that could fail. The arity-3 form additionally never writes `window_type` at all, so it always puts `INVENTORY` on the wire regardless of what the script intended.

**Reconciling the wrapper defect count.** There are exactly **three** `default: break;` sites in the whole 2700-line module: `netSendGiveItemPacket` at `:963-964`, `netSendSafeboxCheckoutPacket` at `:1376-1377`, and the private-shop filter at `:2333`. Only the first two reach a send with an uninitialized scalar, which is why the earlier count of two in this ledger refers to the send-reaching subset rather than to all three sites. I re-verified all three line numbers directly. Both send-reaching cases were already recorded, and the safebox one belongs to the header-77 boundary.

**A second-order defect in the conversion helpers, verified directly.** `PyErr_Occurred` is called **zero** times in `client/Client/ScriptLib/PythonUtils.cpp`; the only `PyErr_*` calls are four `PyErr_Clear` and one `PyErr_SetString`. Combined with the `#define PyLong_AsLong PyLong_AsLongLong` remap at `:3`, a Python argument that is not an integer-convertible object leaves the call returning `true` with `-1` produced and an exception set, so the wrapper's `if (!...)` guard never fires and the send proceeds with `0xFFFFFFFF` or `0xFF`. Worse, `Py_BuildException` at `PythonUtils.cpp:17-34` calls `Py_BuildNone()` at `:32` with the `//return NULL;` line at `:33` **commented out**, so every "error" return in the entire wrapper family hands the script the same value as success. The error path and the success path are literally indistinguishable to the caller. This is pre-existing client behaviour and is not something a Rust codec should reproduce.

**Every narrowing conversion on this path is unchecked, which is why every byte value is a legitimate wire value.** `int` to `BYTE` for the count wraps modulo 256, `int` to `DWORD` for the target wraps modulo 2^32, `int` to `WORD` for the cell goes through the `WORD` overload at `PythonUtils.cpp:119-125` and wraps modulo 65536 so that a `-1` cell is indistinguishable from the default `0xffff`, and `int` to `BYTE` for the window goes through `PyTuple_GetByte` at `:103-109`. No range check exists on any of them.

**A failed send is indistinguishable from success, and the failure window is narrow but real.** The wrapper discards the builder's `bool` at `:968` and returns `Py_BuildNone()` unconditionally at `:969`. `CNetworkStream::Send` at `client/Client/EterLib/NetStream.cpp:783-790` fails only on the capacity check at `:785-787`, and that check includes a `+1`, so the nine-byte record actually needs ten free bytes. `SendSequence` at `:856-859` is an unconditional `return true`, so the builder never reports failure. No encryption happens in `Send`; TEA is applied later at send time.

**The receive side registers the colliding two-byte record, which is a concrete desynchronization hazard.** `HEADER_CG_GIVE_ITEM` and `HEADER_GC_PARTY_PARAMETER` are both 83 in the **same anonymous enum** in the client `Packet.h`, at `:63` and `:167`, so they are genuinely the same compile-time value and no table keyed only on the byte can hold both. The client registers header 83 at `PythonNetworkStream.cpp:114` as `sizeof(TPacketGCPartyParameter)`, that is 2 bytes, statically sized, so inbound 83 is known rather than unknown, and `CheckPacket` uses one function-local static map at `:505` for every phase, so 83 resolves to 2 bytes in all phases. The game phase dispatches it at `PythonNetworkStreamPhaseGame.cpp:496-498` to `RecvPartyParameter` at `:3632-3642`, which delivers `bDistributeMode` to the game window. If a 9-byte give-item record were ever echoed back, the handler would consume bytes 0 and 1, deliver the low byte of `dwTargetVID` to the game window as the party exp-distribution mode, and leave seven bytes to be re-read as the next packet header; if that byte is not registered, the unknown-header path at `PythonNetworkStream.cpp:541` calls `PostQuitMessage(0)` and **the client exits**. The legacy server never does this, so it is recorded as a latent hazard with an explicit note that the current server sends nothing back, not as a live defect. The two debug name tables at `NetStream.cpp:580` and `:680` are separate, so there is no live conflict there, only a readability trap.

**Client items the audit explicitly refused to claim.** The gameplay Python tree is absent from this worktree, so no statement is made about script-side gating. The vendored Python is headers only, so the 64-bit return type of `PyLong_AsLongLong` rests on its declaration rather than on a quoted body. No outcome is asserted for a non-`NULL` C return with a pending exception. And `BYTE`/`WORD`/`DWORD` come from the Windows SDK rather than from a checked typedef in this tree, though on this x86 target they are 1, 2, and 4 bytes, which is what the nine-byte size depends on.


## 142. Selected transport-free `TPacketCGSafeboxCheckout` family record, the first feature-profile-dependent client record width

_Status: selected. This boundary is chosen because it breaks a pattern every earlier slice satisfied, and breaking a pattern safely is worth a dedicated, audited slice.

**The record width depends on a build flag.** `packet.h:1979-1988` declares `typedef struct command_safebox_checkout { BYTE bHeader; #if defined(__EXTENDED_SAFEBOX__) DWORD bSafePos; #else BYTE bSafePos; #endif TItemPos ItemPos; } TPacketCGSafeboxCheckout;`, so the record is **8 bytes** when the flag is defined and **5 bytes** when it is not. This is the first fixed client-to-game record in the item family whose size is not a constant of the source. It is the reason this section must select a feature profile explicitly rather than assume a width, mirroring the rule the DB boot path already follows.

**The flag is defined independently on each side, and the two agree today.** The server defines it at `server/server/common/prodomodefines.h:61` and the client at `client/Client/UserInterface/LOCALE_INC.H:35`, both carrying the same trailing `// __GF_Safebox__` comment. So the active build is 8 bytes on both sides. Nothing enforces that agreement, though: the two are separate translation units in separate trees, so a future build that changed only one would silently produce a 5-versus-8 mismatch. I initially reported that the client never defined the flag; that was wrong, and the cause was my own search, which globbed `*.h` case-sensitively and so missed the uppercase `.H` extension of `LOCALE_INC.H`. No project file under `client/` defines it either, so the header is the only definition site on that side.

**One struct, three header values, one handler.** The server declares only two struct types but registers three headers, and the third reuses the checkout struct outright: `packet_info.cpp:153` sets `HEADER_CG_SAFEBOX_CHECKOUT` to `sizeof(TPacketCGSafeboxCheckout)`, `:154` sets `HEADER_CG_SAFEBOX_CHECKIN` to `sizeof(TPacketCGSafeboxCheckin)`, and `:169` sets `HEADER_CG_MALL_CHECKOUT` to `sizeof(TPacketCGSafeboxCheckout)` as well. The single handler `CInputMain::SafeboxCheckout` at `input_main.cpp:2368-2460` is reached from two of them and is told which by a `bool bMall`: `input_main.cpp:3807` calls it with `false` for the safebox and `:3813` calls it with `true` for the mall. Inside, the flag selects `GetMall()` over `GetSafebox()` at `:2377-2380`, gates Dragon-Soul initialisation at `:2404-2407`, and changes the item-log string between `"MALL GET"` and `"SAFEBOX GET"` at `:2456-2459`. So the **wire record is identical for a safebox withdrawal and a mall withdrawal**, and only the header byte distinguishes them. A codec for this record therefore cannot be named after one container, and a header-keyed lookup table needs three entries that all resolve to the same decoder.

**The header numbering is counterintuitive and must not be guessed.** `HEADER_CG_SAFEBOX_CHECKIN` is **70** and `HEADER_CG_SAFEBOX_CHECKOUT` is **71**, with `HEADER_CG_MALL_CHECKOUT` at 69, so "check in first" is the right instinct and "checkout first" is wrong. All three are identical in the client tree.

**CORRECTED, see the part 3 to 6 record below: all three of 69, 70, and 71 DO collide across directions**, against `HEADER_GC_ADD_FLY_TARGETING`, `HEADER_GC_CREATE_FLY`, and `HEADER_GC_FLY_TARGETING` at `packet.h:157-159` and client `Packet.h:153-155`. The original text of this paragraph claimed no collision, and that claim was produced by a malformed search pattern that matched zero of the 437 header declarations in the file. The original wording is deliberately left visible rather than rewritten, because a silently corrected claim is how the next false claim survives.

**The client already has one of the two wrapper defects characterised in Section 141.** `netSendSafeboxCheckoutPacket` at `client/Client/UserInterface/PythonNetworkStreamModule.cpp:1355-1383` has the same `default: break;` at `:1376-1377` that lets an uninitialised `int iSafeBoxPos` reach the wire, which was recorded in Section 141 as belonging to this boundary rather than to that one.

**Client-side structural difference already confirmed.** The client declares **three** struct types, `command_safebox_checkout`, `command_safebox_checkin`, and `command_mall_checkout` at `client/Client/UserInterface/Packet.h:789`, `:800`, and `:811`, where the server declares only two. The three client structs have byte-identical layouts but name the position field `bSafePos` in two of them and `bMallPos` in the mall one, and each carries its own copy of the same `#if defined(__EXTENDED_SAFEBOX__)` guard. The three server-visible headers are therefore three client struct types and two server struct types, which is a mapping a Rust boundary must state rather than assume.

No code will be written until the ledger records the full contract and the two read-only source audits report; the complete locked/offline workspace gate set and an independent review are required before a completion receipt, as in every earlier section.


### Section 141 Completed: transport-free `TPacketCGGiveItem`, and the final receipt (2026-09-25 15:53 UTC)

**Delivered.** `protocol/src/cg_item_give.rs` encodes and decodes the exact 9-byte legacy record, and `protocol/src/lib.rs` carries the single new `pub mod cg_item_give;` line. The record is `[0x53][target VID: u32 little-endian at 1..5][item position: packed 3-byte at 5..8][item count: u8 at 8]`, and the frame adapter requires exactly 8 payload bytes. The public type is `CgItemGive { target_vid: u32, item_pos: CgItemPos, item_count: u8 }`. The position reuses the shared `CgItemPos` rather than a second offset table, `CG_ITEM_POS_SIZE` is re-exported, and the module stores **no** header field because 0x53 is the only value it can emit. The API is `encode`, `encode_into`, `to_frame`, `decode`, and `decode_frame`, over `CgItemGiveError::{Truncated, LengthMismatch, InvalidHeader}` with `Display` and `std::error::Error`. No inventory or framer change was needed, because the shared inventory already resolved header 83 to `ClientFrameSize::Fixed(9)`.

**Both decoders check the exact length before reading any field and before checking the header.** Short framed payloads are `Truncated`, long ones are `LengthMismatch`, and a wrong header at the correct length is `InvalidHeader`. Every raw wire value round-trips unchanged, including zero and `u32::MAX` identifiers, an unknown window byte, `u16::MAX` cells, a zero and a `u8::MAX` count, and equal source and target positions, which the legacy path does not forbid.

**Audited, and every finding is a documented non-claim rather than a behaviour.** The server handler is `CInputMain::ItemGive` at `input_main.cpp:3174-3183`; the record reaches it from `input_main.cpp:3723-3726` under an observer-only gate. This is **not** a player-to-player give: `CanReceiveItem` returns `false` for any player destination at `char_item.cpp:9255-9256` and `ReceiveItem` repeats the guard at `:9425-9426`. The `byItemCount` byte is a **dead wire field** for this path, read nowhere on it, so it is preserved byte-for-byte and never interpreted. The receiver chooses zero units, exactly one unit, or the whole stack, and there is no ownership check and no same-map check anywhere on the path, only a 2-D distance comparison at `:9259-9260`. The client sends uninitialized stack bytes on a wrong argument count, the server handler is a bare C-style cast with no length, header, or data check, and its `bool` result is discarded.

**Review outcomes.** The independent reviewer built a throwaway crate outside the repository so it could run the real gates and thirteen mutations without touching the worktree. Its verdict on the wire codec itself was clean. All four substantive findings were accepted. Two of them were **real test defects that I reproduced locally before fixing**: deleting the framed header check left all eight tests green, and replacing the byte-at-a-time stream feed with a single bulk feed also left all eight green. Both mutations now fail the intended test, the framed path sweeps every header value at the exact payload length, and the streaming test feeds one byte at a time while asserting `try_decode()` is `None`, that `buffered_len()` tracks the feed, and that `peek_header()` is stable. Two documentation claims were false and are corrected: "the fourth legacy record" is now scoped to the fourth *Rust* codec with the true legacy count of twelve `TPacketCG*` records embedding a packed `TItemPos` stated alongside it, and a test comment that mixed framed-payload and full-wire offset spaces is fixed. While fixing the streaming test I introduced a feed bug of my own and caught it by running the test rather than re-reading it; that is recorded above.
