## 151. `TPacketCGQuickslotDel` and `TPacketCGQuickslotSwap` — headers 17 and 18

The two remaining quickslot records, taken together. They are bundled because
both are fixed-width, neither is variable-length, neither is feature-gated, and
both are the immediate siblings of Section 150's header 16. This also closes the
whole quickslot CG family at headers 16, 17, and 18.

### 151.1 The two records and their widths

`packet.h:26` sets `HEADER_CG_QUICKSLOT_DEL = 17` and `packet.h:27` sets
`HEADER_CG_QUICKSLOT_SWAP = 18`. The declarations are adjacent, at
`packet.h:671-675` and `packet.h:677-682`:

```cpp
typedef struct command_quickslot_del
{
	BYTE	header;
	BYTE	pos;
} TPacketCGQuickslotDel;

typedef struct command_quickslot_swap
{
	BYTE	header;
	BYTE	pos;
	BYTE	change_pos;
} TPacketCGQuickslotSwap;
```

So the two wire records are:

```text
[0x11][pos: u8]                            2 bytes total, 1 after the header
[0x12][pos: u8][change_pos: u8]            3 bytes total, 2 after the header
```

Both sit strictly inside the `#pragma pack(1)` that `packet.h:274` opens and does
not close until `:3540`; those are the only two `#pragma` lines in the file. Four
`#ifdef` pairs do fall between 274 and the declarations, at `:290`/`:292`,
`:486`/`:488`, `:642`/`:647`, and `:649`/`:656`, so the earlier phrasing that
"no `#ifdef` sits between 274 and 690" was **wrong** as written. The conclusion
is unchanged, because the last of those `#endif`s is at `:656`, which is before
`:671`, so the two declarations are outside every conditional. The dispatch arms are
`case HEADER_CG_QUICKSLOT_DEL:` at
`server/server/game/input_main.cpp:3745-3747` and
`case HEADER_CG_QUICKSLOT_SWAP:` at `:3753-3755`. The
`#if defined(__WORLD_BOSS_EVENT__)` at `:3748-3752` sits **between** the two arms
and wraps only `case HEADER_CG_WORLD_BOSS:`, so it does not gate either record;
the swap arm is after its `#endif` at `:3752`. Neither arm touches `iExtraLen`.

Each is registered exactly once, at
`server/server/game/packet_info.cpp:126` and `:127`, as
`Set(HEADER_CG_QUICKSLOT_DEL, sizeof(TPacketCGQuickslotDel), "QuickslotDel")` and
`Set(HEADER_CG_QUICKSLOT_SWAP, sizeof(TPacketCGQuickslotSwap), "QuickslotSwap")`.
The two sizes, 2 and 3, agree with the hand-derived widths. The existing
`protocol/src/cg_inventory.rs` rows already carried `base_size: 2` and
`base_size: 3` with the correct `cpp_type` and `CgPacketRegistration::Registered`,
so **no inventory change was needed**.

### 151.2 Naming: the same capital `S`, and one genuine field drift

The client repeats Section 150's capitalisation. `TPacketCGQuickSlotDel` at
`client/Client/UserInterface/Packet.h:556-560` and `TPacketCGQuickSlotSwap` at
`:562-567` keep the same struct tags `command_quickslot_del` and
`command_quickslot_swap`, the same member counts, and the same 2- and 3-byte
widths, and the client's enumerators at `Packet.h:26` and `:27` also say 17 and
18. The swap record even keeps the **same** field name `change_pos` on both
sides.

The one real field-name drift in this family is on the **outbound** mirror, not
here. The GC quickslot records are declared as bare `struct` rather than
`typedef struct`, at `packet.h:1508-1513`, `:1515-1519`, and `:1521-1526`, and
the server's `packet_quickslot_swap` calls its second field **`pos_to`**, not
`change_pos`. The client agrees with the *server* on that one:
`TPacketGCQuickSlotSwap` in the client also uses `change_pos`. So `pos_to` is
the server's outbound-side outlier, and this codec uses `change_pos`, which is
what both trees call it for the CG record.

The quickslot family across both directions, with widths:

| Direction | Header | Record | Width |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CG | 16 | `TPacketCGQuickslotAdd` | 4 B |
| CG | 17 | `TPacketCGQuickslotDel` | 2 B |
| CG | 18 | `TPacketCGQuickslotSwap` | 3 B |
| GC | 28 | `packet_quickslot_add` | 4 B |
| GC | 29 | `packet_quickslot_del` | 2 B |
| GC | 30 | `packet_quickslot_swap` | 3 B |

### 151.3 Neither handler null-checks the character

This is the defect Section 150.5 flagged in advance, and it is real in both
records. At `input_main.cpp:1116-1126`:

```cpp
void CInputMain::QuickslotDelete(LPCHARACTER ch, const char * data)
{
	struct command_quickslot_del * pinfo = (struct command_quickslot_del *) data;
	ch->DelQuickslot(pinfo->pos);
}

void CInputMain::QuickslotSwap(LPCHARACTER ch, const char * data)
{
	struct command_quickslot_swap * pinfo = (struct command_quickslot_swap *) data;
	ch->SwapQuickslot(pinfo->pos, pinfo->change_pos);
}
```

Compare `QuickslotAdd` at `:1083`, which begins with `if (!ch) return;`. These
two have no such test and dereference `ch` on the first statement. All three are
declared `void` at `input.h:94`, `:95`, and `:96`, and the two new ones each cast `data` straight to
the record without any length argument, and **both discard the `bool` return**
of `DelQuickslot` and `SwapQuickslot`.

Neither arm is behind an `IsObserverMode()` guard, the same as the add arm at
`:3742`. So all three quickslot arms in `Analyze` are unguarded, while their
neighbours `HEADER_CG_ITEM_PICKUP` at `:3715` and `HEADER_CG_USE_SKILL` at
`:3739` are guarded. Recorded, not reproduced.

**Corrected**: the missing `if (!ch)` is *not* reachable as a null dereference,
so calling it a defect overstates it. `Analyze`'s first act at
`input_main.cpp:3647-3652` is `if (!(ch = d->GetCharacter())) { SetPhase(PHASE_CLOSE);
return 0; }`, and each of the two handlers has exactly one call site, so `ch` is
non-null whenever either body runs. The right description is a **style
inconsistency** against its own sibling, not a defect with a trigger.

### 151.4 Both bounds live above the codec, and the character methods differ

`CHARACTER::DelQuickslot(BYTE pos)` is at
`server/server/game/char_quickslot.cpp:100-114` and
`CHARACTER::SwapQuickslot(BYTE a, BYTE b)` at `:116-136`. The bounds are:

- `if (pos >= QUICKSLOT_MAX_NUM) return false;` at `char_quickslot.cpp:104`,
  with `QUICKSLOT_MAX_NUM` 36 at `server/server/common/length.h:51`.
- `if (a >= QUICKSLOT_MAX_NUM || b >= QUICKSLOT_MAX_NUM) return false;` at
  `char_quickslot.cpp:121`.

Neither record's handler checks anything, and **nothing on this record's path
requires the two swap indices to differ**. `SwapQuickslot` copies, assigns, and
assigns back without comparing `a` and `b`, so a self-swap is a legal, if
pointless, request. The claim is scoped to that path on purpose:
`CHARACTER::SyncQuickslot` at `char_quickslot.cpp:14-15` *does* compare two
positions, so "nothing anywhere" would have been too strong.
Both codecs therefore leave their fields as opaque `u8` and neither applies 36,
masks a value, or rejects a self-swap.

The two methods differ from `SetQuickslot` in a way that is a recorded defect
rather than a codec concern: `SetQuickslot` guards with `if (GetDesc())` at
`char_quickslot.cpp:88` before `GetDesc()->Packet(...)` at `:94`, but
`DelQuickslot` at `:112` and `SwapQuickslot` at `:134` call
`GetDesc()->Packet(...)` **unguarded**, while `m_lpDesc` is initialised to
`NULL` at `server/server/game/entity.cpp:27`. Section 150.9 already recorded
this for the delete path via `SetQuickslot`'s own call to `DelQuickslot` at
`:60`; this section confirms the swap record reaches it **directly**, with no
indirection.

Neither codec sends the outbound replies these methods build:
`pack_quickslot_del` at `:109-110` and `pack_quickslot_swap` at `:130-132`,
which use `HEADER_GC_QUICKSLOT_DEL` (29) and `HEADER_GC_QUICKSLOT_SWAP` (30).
The GC direction is a separate boundary and is not touched by this slice.

### 151.5 Collision taxonomy for values 17 and 18

Established with the same enumerator simulator used for Section 150, run over
the same three header enums. The parse counts are identical to Section 150's —
254 enumerators in the server `packet.h`, 218 in server `common/tables.h`, 226
in the client `Packet.h` — and the 15 known-positive controls, including the
auto-incrementing `HEADER_GG_PRIVATE_SHOP_ITEM_SEARCH_RESULT` at 48 and
`HEADER_GG_PRIVATE_SHOP_ITEM_SEARCH_UPDATE` at 50, all reproduce their source
values. **No conditional enumerator carries value 17 or 18**, at any nesting
depth, in any of the three enums.

Every enumerator with value 17:

| Direction | Enumerator | Width | Tree |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CG | `HEADER_CG_QUICKSLOT_DEL` `packet.h:26`, `Packet.h:26` | 2 B | both, live |
| GC | `HEADER_GC_CHARACTER_POINT_CHANGE` `packet.h:117`, `HEADER_GC_PLAYER_POINT_CHANGE` `Packet.h:113` | 25 B | both, **live** (see 151.6) |
| GG | `HEADER_GG_XMAS_WARP_SANTA` `packet.h:246` | 6 B | server only, live |
| GD | `HEADER_GD_SAFEBOX_CHANGE_PASSWORD_SECOND` `common/tables.h:35` | DB-peer framing | server only |

Every enumerator with value 18:

| Direction | Enumerator | Width | Tree |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CG | `HEADER_CG_QUICKSLOT_SWAP` `packet.h:27`, `Packet.h:27` | 3 B | both, live |
| GC | `HEADER_GC_CHANGE_SPEED` `packet.h:118`, `Packet.h:114` | 7 B | **dead on server**, registered on client |
| GG | `HEADER_GG_XMAS_WARP_SANTA_REPLY` `packet.h:247` | 2 B | server only, live |
| GD | `HEADER_GD_DIRECT_ENTER` `common/tables.h:36` | DB-peer framing | server only |

**Inside CG both values are collision-free.** Each names the same struct tag in
both trees, with the same members and the same width. This matches headers 15 and
16.

**Bucket assignment, corrected.** An earlier draft of this subsection called both
values an "inter-direction nominal overlap" and declined to name a bucket. That
was too loose, and it was caused by the same error as 151.6: it assumed GC 17 was
dead. With GC 17 established as **live** at 25 bytes:

- **Value 17 is bucket 2, colliding but not two-sizes.** CG 17 is 2 bytes and GC
  17 is 25 bytes, both live in both trees, both registered. It is not bucket 1,
  because the two trees agree about the CG record's width. It is not bucket 3,
  because 2 and 25 are not equal. It is not bucket 4, because a real struct
  exists on both sides. GG 17 is also live at 6 bytes, so CG 17 and GG 17 must not
  share a table either.
- **Value 18 is bucket 2 for the CG/GG pair** (3 bytes against 2, both live), with
  the server-side GC 18 inert. It is likewise not bucket 1 and not bucket 3. The
  taxonomy's literal bucket-4 wording, "no struct exists", is not satisfied
  because the struct is declared and the client registers it, so 18 is recorded
  as bucket 2 with an inert member rather than forced into bucket 4.

The standing rule is unchanged and is now load-bearing for three adjacent headers
at once: **no header table may mix CG 17 with GC 17, or CG 18 with GC 18.**

Note the direction of the GC hazard is the *opposite* of Section 150's. There,
GC 16 was a 2,041-byte record and a stray 4-byte CG frame would visibly stall.
Here the CG records are the *smaller* side, 2 and 3 bytes against GC's 25 and 7,
so a mixed table would make a CG frame appear to want 22 or 4 more bytes than it
has.

### 151.6 GC 17 liveness: an absence sweep that was wrong, and why

**This subsection originally claimed that both `TPacketGCPointChange` and
`TPacketGCChangeSpeed` are declared and never used. That was wrong about the
first one. GC 17 is live.** The correction is recorded in full because the method
failure is the reusable part.

The original sweep searched for the **typedef alias** `TPacketGCPointChange`
across `server/server` and found one occurrence: its own typedef at
`packet.h:1071`. A one-hit result with positive controls looked convincing. It was
misleading, because the legacy code never spells the alias at these sites. It
declares the local as `struct packet_point_change pack;` and sends it with
`GetDesc()->Packet(&pack, sizeof(struct packet_point_change));`, using the
**struct tag** `packet_point_change` from `packet.h:1064`, not the alias that
`typedef` gives it at `:1071`.

Sweeping the tag instead gives **seven** occurrences, and three send sites:

| site | guard | sends |
|---|---|---|
| `char.cpp:1834-1840` | inside `#ifdef __FIX_UPDATE_PLAYTIME_AND_ITEMS__` (opens `:1833`, closes `:1841`) | `GetDesc()->Packet(&pack, sizeof(struct packet_point_change))` |
| `char.cpp:2093-2116` | **unconditional**; the `#if defined(__CONQUEROR_LEVEL__)` at `:2095` is an extra branch, and the send at `:2116` is outside it, with `#endif` at `:2103` closing the inner block | direct send at `:2116`, `PacketAround` at `:2118` |
| `char.cpp:4805-4818` | **unconditional**, guarded only by `if (GetDesc())` at `:4803` | direct send at `:4818`, `PacketAround` at `:4820` |

Each site sets `pack.header = HEADER_GC_CHARACTER_POINT_CHANGE;` before sending,
so the record is on the wire today, not merely compiled. The client registers it
inbound at `PythonNetworkStream.cpp:70` and reads it at
`PythonNetworkStreamPhaseGame.cpp:1766` and `PythonNetworkStreamPhaseSelect.cpp:146`,
so both ends are active and the record is fully live in the current profile.

`TPacketGCChangeSpeed` / `struct packet_change_speed` at `packet.h:1685-1690` **is**
genuinely dead, and that is now verified in both spellings: the tag
`packet_change_speed` returns one occurrence and the alias
`TPacketGCChangeSpeed` returns one, both being the declaration itself. The client
still registers it inbound at `PythonNetworkStream.cpp:95`. So for value 18 the
dead-server/live-client reader asymmetry is real; for value 17 it is not.

**The method lesson, stated so it can be enforced.** Any "declared but never
used" claim about this legacy tree must sweep the **struct tag** and the typedef
alias as two separate searches, because the two names are not interchangeable in
practice: call sites overwhelmingly use the tag. A single-name sweep returning
one hit is the signature of this failure. Positive controls on the tag name, not
just the alias, are what make the surviving zero result believable. This is now
recorded as a general rule and the earlier claim is treated as withdrawn, not as
a footnote.

**The `int header` quirk is on the wire.** `TPacketGCPointChange` declares its
first member as `int header` rather than `BYTE` at `packet.h:1066`, which under
`#pragma pack(1)` makes that member four bytes and the record
4+4+1+8+8 = 25. Because the record is live, the server writes four little-endian
bytes `11 00 00 00`, not a single `0x11`. The client parses it as an `int` too, so
the two agree and the record works. The earlier text called the observation "moot
while unused"; that is retracted. It is now a live hazard: a future Rust GC 17
codec that copied the one-byte-header convention from its CG 16/17/18 siblings
would be wrong on the very first byte. The GC direction keeps its own framing
convention for this record.

### 151.7 The client senders are clean, and one call site is not bounded

Both client senders are correct. `CPythonNetworkStream::SendQuickSlotDelPacket`
at `client/Client/UserInterface/PythonNetworkStreamPhaseGameItem.cpp:818-835`
guards with `__CanActMainInstance()` at `:820`, assigns both fields at `:825-826`
before sending, and sends `sizeof(TPacketCGQuickSlotDel)`.
`SendQuickSlotMovePacket` at `:837-855` does the same, assigning all three
fields at `:844-846` and sending `sizeof(TPacketCGQuickSlotSwap)`. Every
parameter on both is a `BYTE`, so there is no widening inside either sender. The
log string at `:850` says "SendQuickSlotSwapPacket Error" while the function is
named `SendQuickSlotMovePacket`, a cosmetic mismatch recorded only so it is not
later mistaken for a second sender.

There are **no Python wrappers** for either record, unlike the add record of
Section 150.6; all call sites are in `client/Client/UserInterface/PythonPlayer.cpp`.

The three call sites differ, and the weakest is the swap:

- `RemoveQuickSlotByValue(int iType, int iPosition)` at `PythonPlayer.cpp:899-907`
  iterates a `BYTE i` to `QUICKSLOT_MAX_NUM` and sends
  `SendQuickSlotDelPacket(i)` at `:905`. No narrowing problem, but see 150.7: the
  loop bound is 36, so this path can emit `pos` in 32..35.
- `RequestDeleteGlobalQuickSlot(DWORD dwGlobalSlotIndex)` at `:954-966` bounds-
  checks `dwGlobalSlotIndex >= QUICKSLOT_MAX_COUNT` at `:956` and then sends
  `SendQuickSlotDelPacket((BYTE)dwGlobalSlotIndex)` at `:965`. This is the one
  quickslot call site that is checked against the 32-wide constant.
- `RequestMoveGlobalQuickSlotToLocalQuickSlot(DWORD dwGlobalSrcSlotIndex, DWORD
  dwLocalDstSlotIndex)` at `:917-924` sends
  `SendQuickSlotMovePacket((BYTE) dwGlobalSrcSlotIndex,
  (BYTE)dwGlobalDstSlotIndex)` at `:923` with **no bound check on either
  index**. It is the weakest of the three: the source is unchecked, and the
  destination omits the `QUICKSLOT_MAX_COUNT_PER_LINE` check that its three
  sibling quickslot functions all perform (`:928`, `:939`, `:970`). The helper
  it does call, `LocalQuickSlotIndexToGlobalQuickSlotIndex` at `:862-865`, is
  itself unbounded, and the Python wrapper at `PythonPlayerModule.cpp:1266` reads
  the source as a signed `int` into a `DWORD` and then narrows with `(BYTE)`. A
  script can therefore place any value 0..255 in either slot, including two equal
  values; the server drops the self-swap silently at `char_quickslot.cpp:122`.

**Retracted**: an earlier draft of this subsection claimed a parameter-naming
defect, saying the second parameter is named `dwGlobalDstSlotIndex` and is then
passed to a function expecting a local index. That was wrong. The declaration at
`PythonPlayer.cpp:917` names the parameter `dwLocalDstSlotIndex`; the
`dwGlobalDstSlotIndex` at `:920` is the **local variable derived from it** by
`LocalQuickSlotIndexToGlobalQuickSlotIndex`. The naming is correct and
self-consistent, and `PythonPlayerModule.cpp:1267,1272,1276` agrees by calling
the same value `nLocalDstSlotIndex`. There is no naming defect here.

All three senders are called without checking the returned `bool`, as in
Section 150.6.

### 151.8 Implementation

`protocol/src/cg_quickslot_del.rs` and `protocol/src/cg_quickslot_swap.rs` are
the codecs. Each exposes the full-wire and payload size constants, the record
struct, an error enum with `Truncated`/`LengthMismatch`/`InvalidHeader`, and
`new`, `header`, `encode`, `encode_into`, `to_frame`, `decode`, `decode_frame`.
`protocol/src/lib.rs` gained two `pub mod` lines. `cg_inventory.rs` needed no
change: its rows already resolved both headers, and its content is independently
verified as correct at `:568-574` and `:575-581` (see 151.12). `protocol/tests/cg_wiring.rs` gained one public-surface test per
module, so removing either `pub mod` line is detectable.

There are no `allow(clippy)` suppressions, no packed structs, no `unsafe`, no
`repr(...)`, and no `transmute` in either module.

**A real bug the new tests caught, kept here because the shape recurs.** Both
modules first implemented `decode_frame` by calling the same `check_exact` that
`decode` uses. That helper is calibrated to the **full** record width, but a
`ClientFrame`'s payload **excludes** the header byte, so a correct one-byte
payload was rejected as truncated. Six tests failed on the first run. Each module
now has a second checker, `check_exact_payload`, calibrated to the payload
constant, and `decode_frame` uses it. Any future fixed record with a
header-excluded frame path needs the same split, because the two widths differ
by exactly one.

### 151.11 Handoff: the next numeric CG headers are both profile-dependent

Closing the quickslot family at 16, 17, and 18 does not leave a clean fixed-shape
record next in numeric order, so this is recorded to stop a later continuation
from walking into two conditional records and mistaking them for simple ones.

**Header 22, `HEADER_CG_ITEM_SELL`.** The *enumerator itself* is conditional. At
`packet.h` the CG block reads:

```text
	HEADER_CG_ITEM_DESTROY						= 21,
#ifdef ENABLE_SELL_ITEM
	HEADER_CG_ITEM_SELL							= 22,
#endif
	HEADER_CG_ON_CLICK							= 26,
```

So without `ENABLE_SELL_ITEM` the value 22 names nothing at all, and with it the
record is only present in that profile. The surrounding enumerators are
explicitly assigned, so no other value shifts, but the record's existence and
width are profile-dependent. This is the same conditional that Section 150's
collision audit listed as one of its seven detected conditional enumerators.

**Header 27, `HEADER_CG_EXCHANGE`.** `TPacketCGExchange` at `packet.h` is
`BYTE header; BYTE sub_header;` then a **conditional** `arg1`, then `BYTE arg2`
and a `TItemPos Pos`. The conditional is:

```text
#ifdef ENABLE_REMOVE_LIMIT_GOLD
	unsigned long long arg1;
#else
	DWORD arg1;
#endif
```

so `arg1` is 8 bytes in one profile and 4 in the other, and the record's width
differs by four bytes between them. The record also carries a `sub_header`, so
its dispatch is sub-header dependent rather than a single fixed shape. Its
dispatch arm at `input_main.cpp:3727-3730` is, unlike the three unguarded
quickslot arms, wrapped in `if (!ch->IsObserverMode())`.

**Consequence for the next slice.** A faithful codec for either 22 or 27 has to
select an explicit feature profile and state it, exactly as the DB boot work in
earlier sections does, rather than assuming the active build's defines. Neither
is a good candidate for the next increment unless the profile question is
settled first. This is recorded, not decided here.

A read-only child auditor reviewed this section against the legacy and client
source, with 18 numbered claims to verify or refute, and returned a verdict of

on the receipt. Its report is at `/tmp/agent-reports/sec151_audit.md` (839 lines,
48,201 bytes). It modified nothing under `/workspace` and ran no build.

**Confirmed without change.** Header values and both derived widths; the
`#pragma pack(1)` interval `:274` to `:3540` as the file's only two `#pragma`
lines; exactly one registration per record; the dispatch arms and, critically,
that the `#if defined(__WORLD_BOSS_EVENT__)` at `input_main.cpp:3748-3752` gates
**only** the world-boss case and does not gate the swap arm at `:3753`; the

`GetDesc()` guard asymmetry at `:88` versus `:112` and `:134` with `m_lpDesc`
NULL at `entity.cpp:27`; the absence of Python wrappers, established with a

packed struct, **no** `unsafe`, **no** `repr(`, **no** `transmute`, and **no**
`#[allow(`. The four recorded SHA-256 prefixes are all correct.

**A process failure on my side, recorded because it nearly caused a false
report.** I launched the mutation sweep and the read-only audit **at the same

sweep and a read-only review of the same files must not overlap. The lesson is
recorded rather than the incident.

22 and 27 are feature-gated. `README.md` is 31,523 bytes and 97 lines and now
records 1,160 tests across 28 binaries plus 6 doc-tests, and sections 119-151.

**This section closed the CG quickslot family** at headers 16, 17, and 18. It
also produced one method correction that outlives it: the struct-tag sweep rule in
151.6, which is now a standing rule in `AGENTS.md` because a single-name absence
sweep already produced one false "dead record" claim in this repository.

## 152. CG party family: the five records that complete it

`protocol::cg_party_skill` already covered `TPacketCGPartyUseSkill`. This section
adds the other five party records, which the legacy declares together and
registers together. Together with Section 151 this is the second bundle, chosen
because a bundle is a real unit in this codebase: these six are adjacent in
`packet.h`, contiguous in `packet_info.cpp`, adjacent in the dispatch switch, and
covered by six adjacent client senders.

### 152.1 Declarations, headers, and why all five are fixed-width

| record | declaration | header | line | width |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `TPacketCGPartyParameter` | `packet.h:2004-2008` | `HEADER_CG_PARTY_PARAMETER = 78` | `:62` | 2 |
| `TPacketCGPartyInvite` | `packet.h:2023-2027` | `HEADER_CG_PARTY_INVITE = 72` | `:56` | 5 |
| `TPacketCGPartyInviteAnswer` | `packet.h:2035-2040` | `HEADER_CG_PARTY_INVITE_ANSWER = 73` | `:57` | 6 |
| `TPacketCGPartyRemove` | `packet.h:2071-2075` | `HEADER_CG_PARTY_REMOVE = 74` | `:58` | 5 |
| `TPacketCGPartySetState` | `packet.h:2077-2083` | `HEADER_CG_PARTY_SET_STATE = 75` | `:59` | 7 |

The last conditional before this block is the `#endif` at `packet.h:1997`, and the
first declaration starts at `:2004`, so all five sit outside every `#ifdef`. They
lie strictly inside the `#pragma pack(1)` that `packet.h:274` opens and does not
close until `:3540`. Every width is therefore fixed, and each is corroborated by
the `sizeof` in its own registration.

### 152.2 Wire layouts

```text
72  TPacketCGPartyInvite        [0x48][vid:        u32 little-endian]             5 bytes
73  TPacketCGPartyInviteAnswer  [0x49][leader_vid: u32 little-endian][accept: u8]  6 bytes
74  TPacketCGPartyRemove        [0x4a][pid:        u32 little-endian]             5 bytes
75  TPacketCGPartySetState      [0x4b][pid: u32 little-endian][by_role: u8][flag: u8]  7 bytes
78  TPacketCGPartyParameter     [0x4e][distribute_mode: u8]                        2 bytes
```

`protocol/src/cg_inventory.rs` already carried `base_size` 5, 6, 5, 7, and 2 for
these five rows, and the derived widths match all five, so **no inventory change
was needed**. A wiring test asserts that agreement through the public
`resolve_cg_base_size`, so a future drift in either direction fails the build.

### 152.3 Registration and dispatch

Exactly one registration each, and they are contiguous, at
`server/server/game/packet_info.cpp:146-151`, in the order remove, invite,
invite-answer, set-state, use-skill, parameter. The dispatch arms are equally
contiguous and unconditional at `server/server/game/input_main.cpp:3816-3833`:

| header | arm | call |
|---|---|---|
| 72 | `:3816-3818` | `PartyInvite(ch, c_pData);` |
| 74 | `:3819-3821` | `PartyRemove(ch, c_pData);` |
| 73 | `:3822-3824` | `PartyInviteAnswer(ch, c_pData);` |
| 75 | `:3825-3827` | `PartySetState(ch, c_pData);` |
| `HEADER_CG_PARTY_USE_SKILL` | `:3828-3830` | `PartyUseSkill(ch, c_pData);` |
| 78 | `:3831-3833` | `PartyParameter(ch, c_pData);` |

Not one of the six touches `iExtraLen`, and not one is wrapped in
`IsObserverMode()`, unlike the neighbouring `HEADER_CG_EXCHANGE` arm at `:3727`
and the guarded `HEADER_CG_ITEM_PICKUP` and `HEADER_CG_USE_SKILL` arms. None of
the five new handlers null-checks `ch`; as established in 151.3, that is a style
inconsistency and not a reachable null dereference, because `Analyze` closes the
phase at `input_main.cpp:3647-3652` before any arm runs. All five are declared
`void` at `server/server/game/input.h:118-123`.

### 152.4 Field-name drift between the two trees, including one misnomer

The struct tags are identical in both trees and so are the widths, but the member
names are not. Rust field names follow the server, which is the behavioural
oracle, and the client's names are recorded rather than adopted.

- **`TPacketCGPartyInviteAnswer`**: the server names the second member
  `leader_vid` at `packet.h:2035`; the client names it `leader_pid` at
  `client/Client/UserInterface/Packet.h:838`. Here the **server** is right: it
  resolves the value with `CHARACTER_MANAGER::instance().Find(p->leader_vid)` at
  `input_main.cpp:2507`, which is a virtual-ID lookup.
- **`TPacketCGPartySetState`**: **all four** members differ. Server `header`,
  `pid`, `byRole`, `flag` at `packet.h:2077`; client `byHeader`, `dwVID`,
  `byState`, `byFlag` at `Packet.h:851`. The client's `dwVID` is a **misnomer and
  the substantive finding of this subsection**: the server compares those same
  4 bytes against `pParty->IsMember(p->pid)` at `input_main.cpp:2539` and against
  `ch->GetPlayerID()` at `:2620` and `:2642`, all of which are **player ID**
  spaces. An earlier draft of this sentence cited `GetLeaderPID()` at `:2533` and
  `:2604`; that was wrong. Both of those lines compare the *sender's* party
  leadership, `GetLeaderPID() != ch->GetPlayerID()`, and never read `p->pid`.
  The conclusion is unchanged, but it rests on `:2539`, not on `:2533`.
  The value is a player ID, not a virtual ID, and a future implementation that
  treated it as a VID would look up the wrong object.
- **`TPacketCGPartyUseSkill`**, implemented earlier, drifts the same way: server
  `header`/`vid` against client `byHeader`/`dwTargetVID`.
- `TPacketCGPartyInvite`, `TPacketCGPartyRemove`, and `TPacketCGPartyParameter`
  agree on every member name, including the `b`-prefixed `bHeader` and
  `bDistributeMode` of the last.

### 152.5 What the handlers actually enforce, all of it above framing

Every field stays opaque in the codec. The bounds exist, but every one of them
lives in gameplay code above the record boundary.

- `accept` is a **truthiness** byte. `input_main.cpp:2513` tests `!p->accept`, so
  every non-zero value accepts an invite and only `0` denies. The codec keeps all
  256 values and normalises nothing.
- `by_role` is checked only by a `switch` at `input_main.cpp:2548-2575` whose
  `default` arm merely logs `sys_err` at `:2573`. **`PARTY_ROLE_LEADER` has no
  case arm**: `EPartyRole` at `server/server/game/party.h:15-26` numbers `NORMAL`
  0, `LEADER` 1, `ATTACKER` 2, `TANKER` 3, `BUFFER` 4, `SKILL_MASTER` 5, `HASTE`
  6, `DEFENDER` 7, `MAX_NUM` 8, and the switch covers all of those except
  `LEADER` **and `MAX_NUM`**. An earlier draft said "all except `LEADER`"; the
  sentinel has no arm either, and the enum block begins at `:15`, not `:18`. A client that sends `by_role = 1` therefore reaches the `default` arm
  and gets a log line and nothing else. Recorded, not reproduced.
- `flag` is a truthiness byte, interpolated directly into the `sys_log` format at
  `input_main.cpp:2546` and passed to `SetRole` at `:2559`.
- `distribute_mode` **is** bounded, but above framing:
  `CParty::SetParameter(int iMode)` at `server/server/game/party.cpp:1618-1628`
  rejects `iMode >= PARTY_EXP_DISTRIBUTION_MAX_NUM`, which is 2 in
  `EPartyExpDistributionModes` at `party.h:28-33`, logs
  `sys_err("Invalid exp distribution mode %d")`, and returns without storing. So
  `0` and `1` are valid and `2` through `255` are rejected by the party, and only
  when the sender is a party leader: `prodomodefines.h:89` defines
  `__FIX_EXP_GRUP__`, so the live guard is `input_main.cpp:2767`,
  `ch->GetParty() && ch->GetParty()->GetLeaderPID() == ch->GetPlayerID()`,
  and `:2769` is the `#else` branch. An earlier draft cited `:2769` as the
  guard, which is the inactive side.
- `pid` and `vid` are unchecked 4-byte identifiers. `PartyRemove` compares
  `p->pid` against the sender's own ID at `input_main.cpp:2620` to decide between
  a disband and a kick, and `PartyInvite` feeds `p->vid` straight to
  `CHARACTER_MANAGER::Find` at `:2486`. `0` and `u32::MAX` are both legal.

Nothing above is modelled in Rust. The codecs do not resolve parties, check
leadership, check arena or dungeon state, look up characters, build the
`HEADER_GD_PARTY_STATE_CHANGE` DB request that `input_main.cpp:2566` sends, or
produce any reply.

### 152.6 Collision census for 72, 73, 74, 75, and 78

Two independent methods were run and agree exactly: an enumerator simulator over
all enum blocks, and a tree-wide regex sweep for `HEADER_* = 72|73|74|75|78`.
Both return 13 server enumerators and 10 client enumerators, and no conditional
enumerator carries any of these five values at any nesting depth.

| value | CG | GC (server) | GC (client) | GD |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 72 | `HEADER_CG_PARTY_INVITE` 5 B | `HEADER_GC_SKILL_LEVEL_OLD` | `HEADER_GC_SKILL_LEVEL` | `HEADER_GD_MARRIAGE_REMOVE` |
| 73 | `HEADER_CG_PARTY_INVITE_ANSWER` 6 B | **none** | `HEADER_GC_SKILL_COOLTIME_END` | `HEADER_GD_WEDDING_REQUEST` |
| 74 | `HEADER_CG_PARTY_REMOVE` 5 B | `HEADER_GC_MESSENGER` | `HEADER_GC_MESSENGER` | `HEADER_GD_WEDDING_READY` |
| 75 | `HEADER_CG_PARTY_SET_STATE` 7 B | `HEADER_GC_GUILD` | `HEADER_GC_GUILD` | `HEADER_GD_WEDDING_END` |
| 78 | `HEADER_CG_PARTY_PARAMETER` 2 B | `HEADER_GC_PARTY_ADD` | `HEADER_GC_PARTY_ADD` | **none** |

**Inside CG all five are collision-free**, exactly as headers 15, 16, 17, and 18
were.

**All five are bucket 2, colliding but not two-sizes.** They are not bucket 1,
because both trees agree on each CG record's width. They are not bucket 3,
because no GC record shares a width with its CG sibling. They are not bucket 4,
because real records exist on both sides of every one of these values.

Two of the collisions deserve emphasis because they are the *same subsystem*
pointing the other way. **Value 78 pairs CG `PARTY_PARAMETER` with GC
`PARTY_ADD`**, and **value 75 pairs CG `PARTY_SET_STATE` with GC `GUILD`**, so a
table that mixed directions here would collide between two records from the same
feature. The standing rule is unchanged and now load-bearing for headers 72 to 75
and 78 at once: **no header table may mix CG 72 with GC 72, and so on for 73, 74,
75, and 78.** There is also a one-sided asymmetry at 73, where the client has a
GC record and the server has none, and at 78 in the other direction for GD.

Two naming facts fall out of the table and are recorded so they are not later
mistaken for a port mistake: the server's GC 72 is `HEADER_GC_SKILL_LEVEL_OLD`
while the client calls the same value plain `HEADER_GC_SKILL_LEVEL`, and GC 73
exists only in the client.

### 152.7 The client senders are clean, and the act guard is a file convention

All six party senders are contiguous in
`client/Client/UserInterface/PythonNetworkStreamPhaseGame.cpp:3420-3518`:

| sender | lines | assigns | sends |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SendPartyInvitePacket(DWORD dwVID)` | `:3420-3434` | `header`, `vid` | `sizeof(TPacketCGPartyInvite)` |
| `SendPartyInviteAnswerPacket(DWORD dwLeaderVID, BYTE byAnswer)` | `:3436-3451` | `header`, `leader_pid`, `accept` | `sizeof(TPacketCGPartyInviteAnswer)` |
| `SendPartyRemovePacket(DWORD dwPID)` | `:3453-3467` | `header`, `pid` | `sizeof(TPacketCGPartyRemove)` |
| `SendPartySetStatePacket(DWORD dwVID, BYTE byState, BYTE byFlag)` | `:3469-3485` | `byHeader`, `dwVID`, `byState`, `byFlag` | `sizeof(TPacketCGPartySetState)` |
| `SendPartyUseSkillPacket(BYTE bySkillIndex, DWORD dwVID)` | `:3487-3502` | `byHeader`, `bySkillIndex`, `dwTargetVID` | `sizeof(TPacketCGPartyUseSkill)` |
| `SendPartyParameterPacket(BYTE byDistributeMode)` | `:3504-3518` | `bHeader`, `bDistributeMode` | `sizeof(TPacketCGPartyParameter)` |

Every one assigns all of its fields before sending, sends `sizeof(...)`, and takes
its parameters already at their wire types, so no narrowing happens inside any
sender. None has a defect of the kind Section 150 found in the quickslot add
sender.

**None of them calls `__CanActMainInstance()`.** That guard appears **16** times
in `PythonNetworkStreamPhaseGameItem.cpp`, which holds the quickslot senders, and
**23** times elsewhere in `PythonNetworkStreamPhaseGame.cpp`, which holds all six
party senders. The guard is therefore **not** a per-file convention: it is
applied per sender inside the very file that holds these six, and only the six
party senders omit it. An earlier draft of this paragraph said "0 times in
`PythonNetworkStreamPhaseGame.cpp`" and concluded that the absence was a property
of the file; that count was wrong, and the earlier conclusion with it. What
survives is the narrow and checkable statement: within
`PythonNetworkStreamPhaseGame.cpp` lines 3400-3520 the guard appears **0** times,
while the same file uses it 23 times elsewhere.

### 152.8 Implementation shape, and why one module rather than five

The five codecs live in a single `protocol/src/cg_party.rs`, registered by one
`pub mod cg_party;` line, rather than in five files. Three reasons:

1. The five failure modes are identical, so a single `CgPartyError` replaces five
   near-identical enums. `InvalidHeader` carries the `expected` byte, so the
   `Display` message still names the right record.
2. Headers 72 and 74 are the **same 5-byte shape** with different header bytes, so
   one shared private `check_exact` and one shared private `check_header` remove
   any chance of the two drifting apart.
3. The Section 151 defect, in which `decode_frame` was validated against the full
   record width instead of the payload width, is now **structural**: a single
   private `decode_frame_parts` helper is the only place a frame payload width is
   checked, so the mistake cannot be made a fifth time by copy-paste.

The module exposes, per record, the wire and payload size constants, the record
struct, `header`, `new`, `encode_into`, `encode`, `to_frame`, `decode`, and
`decode_frame`. Both decoders check length before the header, and the header
before any payload byte. All 4-byte fields are written and read through one
private explicit little-endian pair, `write_u32_le` and `read_u32_le`. There are
no packed structs, no `unsafe`, no `repr(...)`, no `transmute`, and no
`#[allow(...)]` anywhere in the module.

A test asserts that `CG_PARTY_INVITE_WIRE_SIZE == CG_PARTY_REMOVE_WIRE_SIZE` and
that decoding one as the other fails with `InvalidHeader`, which is the concrete
reason the header check cannot be dropped for this pair.
### 152.9 Receipt

The closure gates all exited **0**: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, strict
`cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked --offline -- -D warnings`,
`RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --workspace --no-deps --locked --offline`,
`cargo test --workspace --all-targets --no-fail-fast --locked --offline`, and
`cargo test --workspace --doc --no-fail-fast --locked --offline`.

**1,191 tests passed and 0 failed across 28 test binaries, plus 6 workspace
doc-tests.** Every `test result:` line in the captured log was summed rather than
sampled, and no binary reported a failure. Section 151 closed at 1,160, so the
delta is exactly 31: the 29 module tests in `cg_party.rs` plus the 2 new wiring
tests in `cg_wiring.rs`.

Two real defects were found and fixed **by the work itself, before the gates**,
and both are worth recording because each would have shipped silently:

- **`decode_frame` inherited the Section 151 defect class.** The first draft of
  each `decode_frame` validated the frame payload against the **full record
  width** rather than the payload width. Six tests failed as soon as they were
  written, because a correct payload is always one byte shorter than the record.
  The fix is the single shared `decode_frame_parts` helper described in 152.8,
  so the shape is now enforced by construction rather than by review.
- **One of my own tests asserted the wrong expectation.** A case meant to prove
  that a long input with a wrong header reports `LengthMismatch` used a 3-byte
  input, which is *shorter* than the 5-byte record and therefore correctly
  reports `Truncated`. The codec was right and the test was wrong. The test now
  covers both directions, a too-long wrong-header input expecting
  `LengthMismatch` and a too-short wrong-header input expecting `Truncated`, so
  the length-before-header ordering is pinned from both sides.

Strict Clippy also rejected the first draft of one test for five single-character
bindings. That was corrected by naming them, not by adding an `allow`.

The mutation and control results for this section are appended below once the
sweep completes; **no mutation verdict is claimed here**.

**The independent audit is deliberately sequenced after the mutation sweep.**
Section 151 established the rule that a mutation sweep and a read-only review of
the same files must never overlap, because in 151.12 the auditor observed a live
mutation as if it were a real defect. The sweep mutates `cg_party.rs` and
`lib.rs`, which is exactly what an audit of this section must read, so the audit
starts only after restoration is verified.
### 152.10 Mutation results: 19 of 19 caught, and the one survivor was a real gap

Nineteen planned mutations were applied one at a time to `cg_party.rs` and
`lib.rs`, each followed by the **full** no-fail-fast workspace test gate, with
byte-exact restoration through `shutil.copy` and `os.utime` after every case.

The first sweep caught **18 of 19**. The survivor was

```text
P14  encode_into clears the caller buffer
     CgPartyInvite::encode_into gains an out.clear() before its first push
```

This is a **genuine coverage gap and not an equivalent mutation**, so it was
fixed rather than written off. The cause was that the append-semantics test
covered only `CgPartyParameter::encode_into`, so a `clear()` inserted into any
*other* of the five `encode_into` methods changed observable behaviour without
turning any test red. `encode_into` is documented as "Append the record to
`out`", so clearing it would silently discard whatever the caller had already
buffered, which is a real contract violation and not a cosmetic one.

The fix is a family-wide test,
`every_encode_into_appends_and_none_of_them_clears`, which seeds an eight-byte
sentinel, calls all five `encode_into` methods in turn, and requires
`sentinel ++ encoded` each time. Re-running the identical mutation then gives
`CAUGHT`, exit 101, one failed test, failing target `-p protocol --lib`, with the
new test reporting:

```text
assertion `left == right` failed: invite encode_into must append, not clear
  left: [72, 4, 3, 2, 1]
 right: [170, 187, 204, 221, 238, 255, 0, 17, 72, 4, 3, 2, 1]
```

The lesson is recorded because it is a family-level pattern and not a one-off:
**testing a shared contract on one member of a record family does not pin the
contract for its siblings.** Headers 72 and 74 are the same 5-byte shape, and
all five share `check_exact`, `check_header`, and the little-endian helpers, so
any future family that shares an implementation must also share its contract
tests, or must at least be covered by one test per member.

**Final tally: 19 of 19 caught, zero survivors.** Every one of the nineteen
anchors was verified to be present exactly once after restoration, and no
`.mutbak` file remains anywhere in the tree.

The mutations covered all four risk classes that matter for this family:

- **width drift**: P01, P02, P03, P04, P05, P06 move each of the six wire and
  payload size constants by one byte;
- **validation order and strength**: P07 disables the header check, P08 swaps
  length-before-header for header-before-length, and P09 re-introduces the exact
  Section 151 defect by checking a frame payload against the full record width;
- **byte-level fidelity**: P10 and P11 flip the 4-byte fields between little and
  big endian, P12 transposes `by_role` and `flag`, P13 reads `accept` from the
  wrong offset, P15 leaks the header byte into the frame payload, and P14 clears
  the caller's buffer;
- **policy leakage and reachability**: P16 clamps `by_role` to the six roles the
  server switches on, P17 normalises `accept` to a bool, P18 clamps
  `distribute_mode` to three modes, and P19 removes the `pub mod cg_party;`
  line, which is caught only by the public-API wiring tests because no internal
  test can observe the loss of a public module.

### 152.11 Late-binary control

A control mutation was then applied to a file this section never touched,
`world/tests/world_baseline.rs`, changing `assert_eq!(raw_vid, 41)` to
`assert_eq!(raw_vid, 999999)`. It was deliberately placed **after** the whole
sweep so that a stale prebuilt test binary could not mask it.

```text
status CAUGHT, exit 101, failed 1, failing target `-p world --test world_baseline`
```

Restoration of that file was verified afterwards, and no `.mutbak` remained. This
confirms the gate used for the verdict can still observe a failure introduced
