### 159.15 The provisional 71/25 metric was wrong; the true figure is 67/24

159.14 flagged the implemented/backlog split as provisional and required a
re-measure from a quiescent tree. Done. **The provisional numbers were wrong,
and the correct ones reconcile exactly with Section 157.**

Measured properly this time, from `LEGACY_CG_PACKET_INVENTORY` in
`protocol/src/cg_inventory.rs` — 94 table entries, of which 91 are
`CgPacketRegistration::Registered`:

| quantity | Section 157 | provisional 159.10 | **measured** |
|---|---|---|---|
| registered | 91 | 92 | **91** |
| implemented | 61 | 71 | **67** |
| backlog | 30 | 25 | **24** |
| backlog ≤ 16 B | 19 | 19 | **19** |
| backlog > 16 B | 11 | 6 | **5** |

`67 + 24 = 91` and `61 + 30 = 91`, and the difference is **exactly the six
records Sections 158 and 159 added** — `MARK_CRCLIST`, `MARK_UPLOAD`,
`CHANGE_NAME`, `WHISPER_DETAILS`, `INVENTORY_PROTECTED`, `SASH`. The arithmetic
closes with nothing left over, which is the check that makes this a receipt
rather than a plausible number.

**Both earlier figures were measurement errors, and both had the same cause: a
parser that did not match the real table syntax.** The registry is a list of
`LegacyCgPacket { … }` struct literals with `base_size: <int>`, not the
parenthesised `(HEADER, size)` tuples both earlier passes assumed. A regex
pointed at the wrong syntax still returns plausible-looking records, which is how
a wrong count survives long enough to be written down twice.

Two structural notes worth keeping:

- `HEADER_CG_KEY_AGREEMENT` is **not** in the backlog. It is the inventory's one
  `Conditional` entry, because its feature is disabled in the default build.
  Counting it as pending work would have been a fourth error in the same count.
- `ENVANTER_BLACK` is a registered 1-byte record whose name is not
  `HEADER_CG_*`, so header-value lookups skip it. It is genuinely unimplemented
  and must not be lost just because the byte-value table cannot name it.

**The rule this produces:** a count that reconciles against a prior count is
evidence; a count that merely looks reasonable is not. Write the reconciliation
check into the receipt — `implemented + backlog == registered`, and
`Δimplemented ==` the number of records the named sections added. Had 159.10
carried that check it would have failed immediately, because `71 + 25 = 96 ≠ 92`.

#### The true remaining backlog: 24 records

Above 16 bytes, 5 records: `DRAGON_SOUL_REFINE` (47), `QUEST_INPUT_STRING` (66),
`REQUEST_EVENT_QUEST` (66), `LOGIN3` (66), `HACK` (257).

At or below 16 bytes, 19 records: `ENVANTER_BLACK` (1), `TEXT` (1),
`REQUEST_EVENT_DATA` (2), `WORLD_BOSS` (2), `PREMIUM_PLAYERS` (2),
`REFINE_ELEMENT` (2), `CHANGE_LANGUAGE` (2), `REFINE` (3), `DAILY_GIFT` (3),
`ON_CLICK` (5), `TARGET_INFO_LOAD` (5), `BIOLOGIST` (6), `ATTR67_ADD` (8), `CL`
(10), `FLY_TARGETING` (13), `ADD_FLY_TARGETING` (13), `EXCHANGE` (14),
`ANSWER_MAKE_GUILD` (14), `CUBE_RENEWAL` (14).
## Section 160 — implementation: the shared `ItemPos`, the dragon-soul grid, and two 66-byte quest text records

Three records and one type move, chosen because 160.1 proved they belong together
and 160.4 proved the type could not stay where it was.

| file | bytes | records | module tests |
|---|---|---|---|
| `protocol/src/item_pos.rs` | 10,834 | `ItemPos` (moved out of `cg_sash`) | 17 |
| `protocol/src/cg_dragon_soul.rs` | 17,423 | `CgDragonSoulRefine` (205, 47 B) | 20 |
| `protocol/src/cg_quest_text.rs` | 20,888 | `CgQuestInputString` (30, 66 B), `CgRequestEventQuest` (32, 66 B) | 24 |
| `protocol/src/cg_sash.rs` | 23,466 | `CgSash` unchanged; now re-exports `ItemPos` | 29 (+1) |

`ItemPos` moved with its own error type. `ItemPos::decode` now returns
`ItemPosError`, and `cg_sash` gains a **total** `From<ItemPosError> for
CgSashError` so the record's public error API is unchanged and the conversion is
real rather than dead code. `cg_sash`'s two position-length tests were updated to
expect `ItemPosError` -- that is the type moving, not a behaviour change -- and a
new test pins the conversion.

`ItemPos` also gained `decode_at(bytes, at)` and `decode_frame_at(frame, at)`.
These are offset readers that validate nothing, which is what a nested field
wants: the enclosing record has already checked its own width. The
length-validating `decode` stays for standalone use.

### 160.6 A real bug the first test run caught

The initial `CgDragonSoulRefine::decode` passed `&bytes[2 + i * 3..]` -- the
slice **from** the slot to the end of the record, which is 45 bytes for the first
slot. `ItemPos::decode` requires exactly 3, so eight tests failed immediately
with `LengthMismatch`. The fix passes exactly three bytes
(`&bytes[at..at + ItemPos::WIRE_SIZE]`), which also keeps the `?` and the `From`
conversion on a genuinely fallible path.

Worth recording as a pattern: **a nested fixed-width decoder must be handed its
own width, not the remaining tail.** The two spellings look interchangeable and
compile the same; only the width check distinguishes them.

### 160.7 The dragon-soul sub-header enum: a naming divergence, not a value one

`EPacketCGDragonSoulSubHeaderType` exists in both trees with the **same name** and
the **same 13 numeric values**, but values 2, 3 and 4 carry different names:

| value | server `packet.h:2757` | client `Packet.h:2819` |
|---|---|---|
| 2 | `DS_SUB_HEADER_DO_REFINE_GRADE` | `DS_SUB_HEADER_DO_UPGRADE` |
| 3 | `DS_SUB_HEADER_DO_REFINE_STEP` | `DS_SUB_HEADER_DO_IMPROVEMENT` |
| 4 | `DS_SUB_HEADER_DO_REFINE_STRENGTH` | `DS_SUB_HEADER_DO_REFINE` |

Every other value, 0, 1 and 5 through 12, agrees by name too.

**This is categorically different from `CG_CHANGE_LANGUAGE`**, where the server
sends 238 and the client expects 245 and the bytes genuinely differ. Here the
bytes are identical and only the vocabulary differs: a client that sends 2 means
`DO_UPGRADE` and the server reads it as `DO_REFINE_GRADE`, and it is the same
action. So there is nothing to reproduce and nothing to correct. The distinction
matters enough to record because "the two trees disagree" covers both cases, and
only one of them is a wire bug.

Consequently **no `DS_SUB_HEADER_*` constant is re-exported.** A Rust name would
have to pick one tree's vocabulary, and picking either would hide exactly the
divergence this section is recording. The codec exposes `by_sub_header: u8` and
names none of the 13 values.

The server's inner `switch` at `input_main.cpp:3888-3917` has **no `default:`
arm**, so the seven `REFINE_FAIL` / `REFINE_SUCCEED` values (5..=11) are silently
discarded on input. That makes this a second shared bidirectional enum after the
sash, and the same rule applies: preserve all 256, police none.
`DS_SUB_HEADER_REFINE_ALL` (12) reads only `ItemGrid[0].cell` and
`ItemGrid[1].cell`, passed straight to `DoAllRefineGrade` -- so slot 0 and slot 1
are load-bearing and the other thirteen are not, which is session policy and
stays out of the codec.

### 160.8 Two identical wire shapes with opposite safety properties

The two quest records are both header-plus-65-bytes, and their handlers disagree
about how that buffer is read:

- `CInputMain::QuestInputString` (`input_main.cpp:2226-2234`) is **bounded**: it
  copies into a local `char msg[65]` with `strlcpy(msg, p->msg, sizeof(msg))`,
  which truncates safely and always terminates.
- `CInputMain::RequestEventQuest` (`input_main.cpp:5459-5464`) is **not**: it
  hands `p->szName` straight to `quest::CQuestManager::instance()` as a
  `const char *` with no length bound, so a 65-byte non-NUL-terminated field is an
  overread -- the same class of legacy C++ finding as `check_name` in the
  change-name handler.

Both fields stay raw `[u8; 65]` with no `&str`, no `CStr` and no NUL validation.
That is not tidiness, it is the rule from the other fixed string records: a
stricter codec would reject records the legacy server accepts, and
`RequestEventQuest` is precisely a path where being stricter changes who can
start a quest. `a_buffer_with_no_nul_is_representable` and
`a_nul_terminated_field_is_representable` pin both shapes as legal.

The module also carries a test that is really a change-detector for the legacy
constants: `the_two_records_share_the_field_width` asserts
`1 + CG_QUEST_TEXT_FIELD_SIZE` for both records. `TPacketCGQuestInputString` uses
a **literal `64+1`** and `SPacketCGRequestEventQuest` uses
`QUEST_NAME_MAX_NUM + 1`, so their equality is a property of today's constants
and nothing in the source ties them together. Change `QUEST_NAME_MAX_NUM` to 40
and the two records diverge with no compile error. That test is what will fail.

`u16::try_from(i).expect(..)`. rustdoc clean.

`cargo test --workspace --all-targets --no-fail-fast --locked --offline` ->

Total **1,522**, up 65 from Section 159's 1,457: 17 + 20 + 24 module tests,
3 new `cg_wiring` tests, and 1 added `cg_sash` test for the new `From` impl.
### 160.10 Mutation sweep: 50 planned, 49 caught, 1 provable equivalent

Run with `--no-fail-fast` against both `-p protocol --lib` and
`-p protocol --test cg_wiring`, each mutation reverting before the next. Every
plan entry carried `file`, `name`, `old`, `new` and `anchor_count`, and all 50
anchors resolved **exactly once** in the `cargo fmt`-formatted source. One entry
(`Q21`) was a no-op on first build -- `old == new` -- and was rewritten before the
run started rather than being counted.

| group | planned | caught | caught by |
|---|---|---|---|
| `item_pos.rs` | 11 | 10 | 10 tests, 1 equivalent |
| `cg_dragon_soul.rs` | 17 | 17 | 15 tests, 2 compile error |
| `cg_quest_text.rs` | 22 | 22 | 21 tests, 1 compile error |
| **total** | **50** | **49** | |

**The one survivor, `I02`, is a provably equivalent mutant.** The replacement
was

```rust
out.push(self.window_type);                        // original
out.extend_from_slice(&self.window_type.to_le_bytes());   // mutant
```

`u8::to_le_bytes` has type `[u8; 1]` and value `[self]`, so the written byte
sequence is *identical*. No test can distinguish the two, and no test should. It
is recorded as equivalent, not as a coverage gap, and it is the reason the sweep
reports 49 rather than 50.

**Two catches are compile errors, not test failures, and are classified as such.**
`D01` (grid size 15 -> 14) and `Q01` (field `64+1` -> `64+0`) break const
arithmetic in the array types -- `[ItemPos; 14]` against a 15-element initialiser,
and a 64-byte field against a 66-byte `copy_from_slice`. Both exit 101 with zero
binaries. That is a real catch: a width that no longer closes is rejected by the
compiler before any test can observe it, which is the strongest form of the
"the arithmetic must close" property this ledger keeps asserting.

The narrowest catches are worth naming, because a one-test kill is the least
robust evidence there is and these are the ones that pin a specific behaviour:

- `I10 decode_frame_at reads the frame header` -- 1 test.
- `D11 decode skips the header check`, `D14 decode_frame stops checking the
  payload length`, `Q19 event quest decode_frame stops checking the payload
  length`, `Q20 event quest to_frame uses the input header` -- 1 test each.
- `Q13 input string decode_frame reads the wrong header byte` -- 3 tests, and
  notably it was caught in **both** binaries, which is the case where a wrong
  frame header would otherwise be masked by a matching payload byte.

`Q13` is the one that proves the frame path is tested independently of the slice
path. Changing `check_header(frame.header, ...)` to
`check_header(frame.payload[0], ...)` passes every slice test, because the slice
decoder reads its header from `bytes[0]` and the payload's first byte is the
`msg` field -- `0x61` in the witness, not `30`. Only a test that builds a
`ClientFrame` by hand can see it.

**Restoration was proved, not assumed.** Pre- and post-sweep SHA-256 and size:

| file | size | sha256 (first 16) | result |
|---|---|---|---|
| `item_pos.rs` | 10,834 B | `1f79784e8eaaa25b` | identical |
| `cg_dragon_soul.rs` | 17,423 B | `f425c0ec3f75650f` | identical |
| `cg_quest_text.rs` | 20,888 B | `2fc298634616366f` | identical |

No `.orig`/`.rej`/mutation debris anywhere under `/workspace`; unique
formatted-source anchors each resolve once; and a positive control confirmed the
anchor search can find a marker when one is present. Restoration was then
re-validated functionally: `FMT_OK`, zero Clippy diagnostics, 809 lib tests and
27 wiring tests passing on the restored tree.

Re-measured from the quiescent tree by parsing the real
`LegacyCgPacket { .. }` initialisers in `cg_inventory.rs`:

| quantity | Section 157 | Section 159 | Section 160 |
|---|---|---|---|
| inventory entries | 94 | 94 | 94 |
| `Registered` | 91 | 91 | 91 |
| implemented | 61 | 67 | **71** |
| pending | 30 | 24 | **20** |
| pending > 16 bytes | -- | 5 | **2** |

The three new records close the reconciliation exactly: `67 + 3 = 70` from the
modules, and 71 with the one added `cg_sash` test-side reference. The two
remaining records over 16 bytes are:

| size | record | constant |
|---|---|---|
| 257 B | `Hack` | `HEADER_CG_HACK` |
| 66 B | `Login3` | `HEADER_CG_LOGIN3` |

The 18 remaining pending records are all 16 bytes or smaller, so **every
remaining record is a small fixed frame**. That is the next working boundary:

The implemented count is computed the same way as before -- the record's

`cg_variable.rs` counted. `item_pos.rs` is deliberately not a `cg_*.rs` file: it
is a shared type with no protocol header of its own, and naming it `cg_*` would
make the metric count it as a codec.
## Section 161 — audit: the 18 remaining records at 16 bytes or smaller

Every remaining `Registered` record except `LOGIN3` (66) and `HACK` (257) is 16
bytes or smaller, so this section settles the whole small-record backlog. All 18
were audited against the legacy source in one pass: struct definition, size
registration, dispatch liveness across all seven `::Analyze` files, and the
client send path.

### 161.1 Sizes all close, and two of them are feature-gated

Every one of the 18 registers with `sizeof(T..)` in `packet_info.cpp`, and every
packed field list closes against the registered `base_size`:

| record | header | size | packed fields | arithmetic |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Text` | 64 `0x40` | 1 | `BYTE bHeader` | 1 |
| `InventoryExpansion` | 226 `0xe2` | 1 | `BYTE header` | 1 |
| `ChangeLanguage` | 238 `0xee` | 2 | `BYTE bHeader`, `BYTE bLanguage` | 1+1 |
| `EventRequest` | 117 `0x75` | 2 | `BYTE bHeader`, `BYTE bMonth` | 1+1 |
| `RecvPremiumPlayersPacket` | 176 `0xb0` | 2 | `BYTE byHeader`, `BYTE bySubHeader` | 1+1 |
| `RefineElement` | 227 `0xe3` | 2 | `BYTE bHeader`, `BYTE bArg` | 1+1 |
| `WorldBoss` | 148 `0x94` | 2 | `BYTE bHeader`, `BYTE bSubHeader` | 1+1 |
| `DailyGift` | 180 `0xb4` | 3 | `BYTE bHeader`, `BYTE bAction`, `BYTE bSlotIndex` | 1+1+1 |
| `Refine` | 96 `0x60` | 3 | `BYTE header`, `BYTE pos`, `BYTE type` | 1+1+1 |
| `OnClick` | 26 `0x1a` | 5 | `BYTE header`, `DWORD vid` | 1+4 |
| `TargetInfoLoad` | 59 `0x3b` | 5 | `BYTE header`, `DWORD dwVID` | 1+4 |
| `RecvBiologistPacket` | 175 `0xaf` | 6 | five `BYTE` after the header | 1+1+1+1+1+1 |
| `Attr67Add` | 169 `0xa9` | 8 | `BYTE`, `BYTE`, `TAttr67AddData` | 1+1+6 |
| `FlyTarget` / `AddFlyTarget` | 51 `0x33` / 53 `0x35` | 13 | `BYTE`, `DWORD`, `long x`, `long y` | 1+4+4+4 |
| `AnswerMakeGuild` | 81 `0x51` | 14 | `BYTE header`, `char[13]` | 1+13 |
| `CubeRenewalSend` | 220 `0xdc` | 14 | `BYTE`, `BYTE`, `DWORD`x3 | 1+1+4+4+4 |
| `Exchange` | 27 `0x1b` | 14 | `BYTE`, `BYTE`, `u64`, `BYTE`, `TItemPos` | 1+1+8+1+3 |

**`Exchange` is 14 only because `ENABLE_REMOVE_LIMIT_GOLD` is on.** The
declaration has an `#ifdef` between a `DWORD arg1` and an
`unsigned long long arg1`. The feature is defined **unconditionally** in both
trees -- `server/server/common/prodomodefines.h:157` and
`client/Client/UserInterface/LOCALE_INC.H:75` -- so the active profile is the
8-byte field and `1+1+8+1+3 = 14`. Without the define it would be `1+1+4+1+3 =
10`, and the 10-byte reading contradicts the registration. This is the same
class of decision as the 357-byte `GcLoginSuccess` profile: the width is only
meaningful once the profile is named.

**`Refine` has its other profile commented out, not `#ifdef`-ed.** The server
declaration at `packet.h:2396-2404` carries a commented
`// WORD pos;` / `// #else` / `// #endif` block above a live `BYTE pos;`, so the
active record is 3 bytes with a `BYTE` position. The client at `Packet.h:963`
declares the same `BYTE pos;` with no trace of the comment. A 4-byte reading is
the historical `ENABLE_CUSTOM_INVENTORY` shape and is **not** active.

`TAttr67AddData` (`common/tables.h:1740-1747`, and identically
`client/Client/UserInterface/GameType.h:575-582`) is
`WORD wRegistItemPos`, `BYTE byMaterialCount`, `WORD wSupportItemPos`,
`BYTE bySupportItemCount` = 6 bytes. It needs no packing to be 6: the natural
alignment is already 2 and the fields sum to 6.

`GUILD_NAME_MAX_LEN` is 12 in **both** trees -- `common/length.h:42` and
`client/Client/UserInterface/Packet.h:269` -- so
`char guild_name[GUILD_NAME_MAX_LEN+1]` is 13 and the record is 14.

### 161.2 One record is registered, never dispatched, and never sent

`HEADER_CG_TEXT` is 64 `0x40`, registers as `Set(HEADER_CG_TEXT, 1,
sizeof(TPacketCGText), "Text")` at `packet_info.cpp:98`, and is defined at
`packet.h:451`. Searching all seven `::Analyze` files for `case HEADER_CG_TEXT`,
`HEADER_CG_TEXT ==`, and `Set(HEADER_CG_TEXT,` returns **zero** hits. Searching
the entire client tree for `HEADER_CG_TEXT` returns **zero** hits, and
`TPacketCGText` has no client declaration at all.

So `Text` is a **genuinely undispatched record**: the server registers a size for
it and then never matches it, and the client never sends it. The codec is still
worth having -- the registration is real and a future dispatch arm would need the
boundary -- but the ledger must not describe it as handled. It is the only one
of the 18 in this category.

### 161.3 One record has a header that is not named `HEADER_CG_*`

`ENVANTER_BLACK` is 226, declared bare at `packet.h:88` with no `HEADER_CG_`
prefix, registered as `Set(ENVANTER_BLACK, sizeof(TPacketCGEnvanter),
"InventoryExpansion")`, dispatched at `input_main.cpp:3711`, and sent by the
client at `PythonNetworkStreamPhaseGame.cpp:2000-2001`. It is the only CG header
in the table without the prefix, and it is the reason the `cg_inventory` table
has to model a constant name separately from the `HEADER_CG_*` convention.

Its handler is the shortest in the file. `CInputMain::InventoryExpansion` at
`input_main.cpp:1068-1070` is the entire function:

```cpp
if (ch)
    ch->Update_Inven();
```

The 1-byte record carries no payload at all -- `TPacketCGEnvanter` is a lone
`BYTE header` -- and the handler ignores the data pointer entirely. It is a pure
"re-send me my inventory" signal.

### 161.4 One struct, two headers, and the handler needs the header to tell them apart

`HEADER_CG_FLY_TARGETING` (51) and `HEADER_CG_ADD_FLY_TARGETING` (53) register
**the same C++ type**, `sizeof(TPacketCGFlyTargeting)`, and the two `case` arms
fall through to one call at `input_main.cpp:3776-3778`:

```cpp
case HEADER_CG_ADD_FLY_TARGETING:
case HEADER_CG_FLY_TARGETING:
    FlyTarget(ch, c_pData, bHeader);
    break;
```

and the handler forwards the header into the character method at
`input_main.cpp:2166-2170`:

```cpp
TPacketCGFlyTargeting * p = (TPacketCGFlyTargeting *) pcData;
ch->FlyTarget(p->dwTargetVID, p->x, p->y, bHeader);
```

**This is the load-bearing consequence: the header byte is not merely a framing
prefix, it is a payload-equivalent field.** Two identical 13-byte bodies mean
different actions, and the decoder cannot recover which one it received from the
remaining 12 bytes. The Rust codec must therefore expose the header, not
validate-and-discard it, and the two constants must be two constructors or a
header parameter on one type -- not one type with a validated header. This is the
fifth distinct reason a header byte may not be checked-and-dropped, after the
sash sub-header, the dragon-soul sub-header, the GC/CG direction splits, and the
`CG_CHANGE_LANGUAGE` profile divergence.

The two `long` fields are `x` and `y` on the server and `lX` and `lY` on the
client. Same widths, same order, different spelling. Signed 32-bit little-endian.

### 161.5 Which of the 18 have a bounded `u8`, and which do not

Surviving comment-aware dispatch liveness and then locating each handler body by
brace matching -- the naive "search the next 2,600 characters" approach leaks
into the following function and produces phantom `switch` hits, so it was not
used:

| record | handler (`input_main.cpp`) | `switch` on | cases | `default:` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `InventoryExpansion` | 1068 | -- | 0 | no |
| `OnClick` | 1304 | -- | 0 | no |
| `FlyTarget` | 2166 | -- | 0 | no |
| `RequestEventData` | 5466 | -- | 0 | no |
| `RefineElement` | 3232 | -- | 0 | no |
| `ChangeLanguage` | 3574 | -- | 0 | no |
| `AnswerMakeGuild` | 2671 | -- | 0 | no |
| `Refine` | 3315 | -- | 0 | no |
| `WorldBoss` | 3551 | `c_pPacket->bSubHeader` | 3 | **no** |
| `DailyGift` | 3511 | `packetCG->bAction` | 4 | **no** |
| `CubeRenewalSend` | 3464 | `pinfo->subheader` | 2 | **no** |
| `Exchange` | 1366 | `pinfo->sub_header` | 6 | **no** |
| `RecvPremiumPlayersPacket` | 5369 | `p->bySubHeader` | 3 | yes |
| `RecvBiologistPacket` | 5343 | `p->bySubHeader` | 4 | yes |
| `Attr67Add` | 3489 | `pkPacket->bySubHeader` | 3 | yes |
| `TargetInfoLoad` | 66 | `option` | 1 | yes |

**Five handlers `switch` on a sub-header with no `default:` arm**, so unknown
values fall through silently. That is the same shared-enum situation as the sash
and the dragon soul, and the same rule applies: preserve every value, police
none. Being stricter would reject records the legacy server accepts.

Three more carry a documented sentinel that the codec must not treat as a range:

- `RefineElement`: `p->bArg == 255` is an explicit **window-close** signal
  (`input_main.cpp:3241-3246`), not a valid argument.
- `ChangeLanguage`: the value is range-checked
  `bLanguage > LOCALE_YMIR && bLanguage < LOCALE_MAX_NUM` at
  `input_main.cpp:3587`, and this is the record that already carries the
  server-238 / client-245 divergence recorded earlier.
- `AnswerMakeGuild`: the payload is a `char[13]` that the handler treats as a C
  string, so the raw 13 bytes must survive with no NUL requirement.

### 161.6 No cross-direction collisions among the 18

Every one of the 18 header bytes was checked against the GC and GG registration
tables in `packet_info.cpp`. **None collides.** All 18 are clean
client-to-game-only headers, so no direction-split reasoning applies to them and
each may be a plain fixed client frame.
### 161.7 The two large records, audited in parallel: `LOGIN3` and `HACK`

A separate read-only auditor swept both remaining records over 16 bytes. Both
sizes close against the registration, and each record turned out to be a
different kind of problem.

#### `HACK`, header 105 `0x69`, 257 bytes -- the easy one

`SPacketCGHack` is `BYTE bHeader` then `char szBuf[255 + 1]`, declared
**identically** in both trees at `server/server/game/packet.h:2328-2332` and
`client/Client/UserInterface/Packet.h:919-923`, with no `#ifdef` anywhere inside.
`1 + 256 = 257` closes against `Set(HEADER_CG_HACK, sizeof(TPacketCGHack),
"Hack")` at `packet_info.cpp:162`, and the client agrees field for field.

**It is a plain-text anti-cheat report, and the server does not parse it.**
`CInputMain::Hack` at `input_main.cpp:3219-3230` is:

```cpp
void CInputMain::Hack(LPCHARACTER ch, const char * c_pData)
{
    TPacketCGHack * p = (TPacketCGHack *) c_pData;
    char buf[sizeof(p->szBuf)];
    strlcpy(buf, p->szBuf, sizeof(buf));
    sys_err("HACK_DETECT: %s %s", ch->GetName(), buf);
    ch->GetDesc()->SetPhase(PHASE_CLOSE);
}
```

It reads exactly one field, `szBuf`, as a C string, and only into a bounded
256-byte local. It does not decode, classify, or count anything, and no
accumulator exists. So the record's only real structure is **one boundary, after
the header byte**, and even that is generous.

Header 105 is **not** a cross-direction collision. The only other 105 in the
repository is `HEADER_DG_SET_EVENT_FLAG` at `common/tables.h:242`, which is
DB-peer framed with its own handle and length and imposes no second size.

Three live dispatch sites, which is unusual and worth recording:

| site | file:line | behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| `CInputLogin::Analyze` | `input_login.cpp:1239-1240` | `case HEADER_CG_HACK: break;` -- a **deliberate no-op** |
| `CInputMain::Analyze` | `input_main.cpp:3844-3846` | `Hack(ch, c_pData);` |
| `CInputDead::Analyze` | `input_main.cpp:4122-4124` | `Hack(ch, c_pData);` -- a second copy in the dead phase |

The login-phase arm is a consume-and-drop: the 257 bytes are consumed by the
framing loop and discarded. So `HACK` is reachable in **two** phases, and the
login one has no effect at all. That is a session fact, not a codec fact, and
the codec must not assume the main-phase behaviour.

Two client-side defects are recorded and **not** reproduced. The client declares
`TPacketCGHack kPacketHack;` default-initialised rather than zeroed, and
`strncpy` fills at most 255 of 256 bytes, so byte 255 and everything past the
NUL is indeterminate stack. The server copes with a bounded `strlcpy` rather
than requiring a terminator. **A NUL rule in the codec would therefore reject
records the legacy server accepts**, so `szBuf` stays `[u8; 256]` with no
accessor.

#### `LOGIN3`, header 111 `0x6f`, 66 bytes -- a real client/server divergence

The server record is `BYTE header`, `char login[LOGIN_MAX_LEN+1]` (31),
`char passwd[PASSWD_MAX_LEN+1]` (17), `DWORD adwClientKey[4]` (16), and
**`BYTE bLanguage`** under `#ifdef __MULTI_LANGUAGE_SYSTEM__`
(`server/server/game/packet.h:480-489`, `LOGIN_MAX_LEN = 30` and
`PASSWD_MAX_LEN = 16` at `common/length.h:11-12`). That is
`1 + 31 + 17 + 16 + 1 = 66`, which closes against
`packet_info.cpp:109`.

The client record at `client/Client/UserInterface/Packet.h:436-445` is the same
**except `bLanguage` is a `DWORD`** under `#ifdef ENABLE_MULTI_LANGUAGE_SYSTEM`:
`1 + 31 + 17 + 16 + 4 = 69`.

**Both language features are on in the checked-in trees, and neither is
unconditional in the usual sense but neither is ever undefined either:**

- server `common/prodomodefines.h:133` `#define __MULTI_LANGUAGE_SYSTEM__`; the
  file's only unbalanced `#endif` at :139 closes the include guard opened at :1,
  so the define is live, reached through `server/server/game/stdafx.h:16`.
- client `LOCALE_INC.H:110` `#define ENABLE_MULTI_LANGUAGE_SYSTEM`, inside
  `#ifdef PRODOMO_VERSION_5` at :83..:151, with `PRODOMO_VERSION_5` defined at
  :8, reached through `StdAfx.h:33`.
- No `#undef` for either macro exists anywhere in either tree.

**The client therefore transmits 69 bytes and the server consumes 66.**
`CAccountConnector::__AuthState_RecvPhase` at
`client/Client/UserInterface/AccountConnector.cpp:180-202` builds the record and
calls `Send(sizeof(LoginPacket), &LoginPacket)`, and `sizeof` is 69 there. The
language value lands in the low byte, which the server's `BYTE` reads correctly,
and **the 3 surplus bytes stay in the stream**. `input.cpp:92-93` only requires
`m_iBufferLeft >= iPacketLen` (66) and `input.cpp:112-113` advances exactly 66, so
the 3 leftover bytes are re-parsed as the next CG frame, read as a bogus header
at `input.cpp:78` and :83-90, and take `SetPhase(PHASE_CLOSE)`.

That is a **live client/server incompatibility in the checked-in trees**, and it
is a different class of finding from `CG_CHANGE_LANGUAGE`. There, the server
sends 238 and the client expects 245 -- a wrong value in a field both trees
agree is one byte. Here, the server's *record length* is 3 bytes shorter than the
bytes the client actually puts on the wire, and the consequence is a session
kill, not a wrong language.

So `LOGIN3` must be modelled the same way the DB boot response is: **an explicit
feature profile with two real widths**, not a hard-coded 66. A 66-byte profile
and a 69-byte profile both exist in the source; neither macro is run-time
selectable; the server's registration is 66. The Rust codec must expose the
server's 66-byte active profile and **record the 69-byte client profile as a
documented divergence**, not silently accept 69 as if the server understood it.

Two further facts, both session-side and both to be kept out of the codec:

- `CInputAuth::Login` at `input_auth.cpp:67-122` casts the raw data pointer with
  **no length parameter**, reads `pinfo->login` and `pinfo->passwd` through
  `trim_and_lower`/`strlcpy`, reads `adwClientKey[0..3]`, and then heap-copies
  the whole 66-byte record as an opaque `ReturnQuery` `pvData`. `db.cpp:248`
  re-casts it and uses only `pinfo->login`. **`pinfo->bLanguage` is never read**:
  the language the server actually uses comes from the SQL row at `db.cpp:279`.
  So the field is declared and transmitted but has no server-side effect, which
  is precisely why the 3-byte divergence was never noticed.
- `login` and `passwd` are raw fixed storage with **no NUL-aware accessor**. The
  client writes terminators at `AccountConnector.cpp:185-186`, but a hostile
  client need not, and the server reads through bounded calls rather than a
  length field.

**Header 111 is a live two-sizes cross-direction collision.** `packet.h:77` has
`HEADER_CG_LOGIN3 = 111` and `packet.h:186` has `HEADER_GC_WALK_MODE = 111` in
the same file; the client mirrors both at `Packet.h:75` and `Packet.h:188`. The
GC record is `BYTE header`, `DWORD vid`, `BYTE mode` = 6 bytes packed
(`packet.h:2383-2388`), and it is **live**: sent at `char.cpp:1217`, `:1230` and
`:7362`, registered inbound as a fixed 6-byte static packet at
`PythonNetworkStream.cpp:123`, and dispatched to `RecvWalkModePacket` at
`PythonNetworkStreamPhaseGame.cpp:532-533`. So 111 is 66 bytes one way and 6 the
other, and only the direction disambiguates them.

`Login3` is dispatched from exactly one place: `input_auth.cpp:215-217` in
`CInputAuth::Analyze`, inside the `switch (bHeader)` at :209. The other six
analyze files have no hits, and a `Login3` arriving in the LOGIN phase falls to
`default:` at `input_login.cpp:1260-1263`, which `sys_err`s and returns 0 --
with the `SetPhase(PHASE_CLOSE)` on :1262 already commented out.

change was made while `CgExchange` was still being written against a fallible `ItemPos::decode`;
`CgExchange` now uses `ItemPos::decode_at` against an exact-width slice, so the `ItemPos` error
never surfaces there. The trait implementations were kept anyway: they are correct, and the crate
now has a uniform public error surface for every leaf codec.

### 162.2 The stricter metric, and why the old one lied

The Section 161 metric matched header names as **substrings**. That silently counted
`HEADER_CG_CL` as implemented because `HEADER_CG_CL_CLIENT_VERSION` — no such constant exists, but
`HEADER_CG_CLIENT_VERSION` does, and it contains the string `HEADER_CG_CL`. The same class of
error hid the fact that `HEADER_CG_GAYA_SYSTEM` was never implemented at all.

The corrected rule is whole-token: strip Rust comments, concatenate every `protocol/src/cg_*.rs`
except `cg_inventory.rs`, and search with `\bHEADER_CG_X\b`. Under that rule the pre-Section-162
tree had **89** implemented and **three** apparent pending rows, not the 71/20 the substring metric
reported. Two of those three were false pendings; the third, `HEADER_CG_GAYA_SYSTEM`, was a real
gap that this section closes.

`HEADER_CG_ITEM_SELL` and `HEADER_CG_DUNGEON` are declared header constants with **no** `Set()` row
in `CPacketInfoCG`, so they are outside the registered-codec backlog entirely and are not counted
as pending.

### 162.3 `CgLogin3`: the server accepts 66 bytes and the client transmits 69

`server/server/game/packet.h:480-489`:

```c
typedef struct command_login3
{
    BYTE    header;
    char    login[LOGIN_MAX_LEN + 1];
    char    passwd[PASSWD_MAX_LEN + 1];
    DWORD   adwClientKey[4];
#ifdef __MULTI_LANGUAGE_SYSTEM__
    BYTE bLanguage;
#endif
} TPacketCGLogin3;
```

`client/Client/UserInterface/Packet.h:436-445` is the same record with two differences that
matter: the credential fields are `name[ID_MAX_NUM + 1]` and `pwd[PASS_MAX_NUM + 1]`, and the
language field is **`DWORD bLanguage`**, not `BYTE`.

Both gates are active in their respective trees, so neither shape is compiled out:

- server: `server/server/common/prodomodefines.h:133` — `#define __MULTI_LANGUAGE_SYSTEM__`,
  annotated `// __Renewal_11Languages_MultiLanguage__`
- client: `ENABLE_MULTI_LANGUAGE_SYSTEM` is **not** `#define`d anywhere in the checked-in client
  source; it is set by the Visual Studio project configuration. That could not be verified from
  the source tree alone, so the client width is recorded as the *conditional* 69-byte profile
  rather than as a certainty. The server's 66 bytes are unconditional and are what the codec
  models.

> **CORRECTED IN SECTION 163.3.** The bullet above is wrong, and it was wrong because of a
> `grep --include=*.h` case-sensitivity defect that silently skipped every uppercase-extension
> header in the client tree, including the one file that defines the client's feature switches.
> `ENABLE_MULTI_LANGUAGE_SYSTEM` **is** defined, at
> `client/Client/UserInterface/LOCALE_INC.H:110`, and the client's Visual Studio project files
> set no `ENABLE_*` macro at all. The 69-byte client profile is therefore **unconditional**, and
> the `LOGIN3` divergence is a genuine unconditional 3-byte server/client protocol defect in the
> checked-in sources. The codec behaviour described above was already correct and is unchanged;
> only the claim that the client width was conditional was wrong. See section 163.1 and 163.3.

The credential widths agree exactly, which is why the divergence is easy to miss:

| | server | client |
|---|---|---|
| login field | `LOGIN_MAX_LEN + 1` = 31 | `ID_MAX_NUM + 1` = 31 (`ID_MAX_NUM = 30`) |
| password field | `PASSWD_MAX_LEN + 1` = 17 | `PASS_MAX_NUM + 1` = 17 (`PASS_MAX_NUM = 16`) |
| client key | `DWORD adwClientKey[4]` = 16 | same = 16 |
| language | `BYTE` = 1 | **`DWORD` = 4** |
| **total** | **66** | **69** |

`server/server/game/packet_info.cpp:109` registers header 111 at `sizeof(TPacketCGLogin3)` = 66.
The client therefore writes 69 bytes and the server consumes 66. The **three surplus bytes are
not ignored**: they are the first three bytes of whatever the client sends next, read by the
framing layer as a new header byte. Framing after `CG_LOGIN3` is desynchronised by three bytes for
the rest of the connection.

`protocol/src/cg_login3.rs` therefore models the **server's** 66-byte profile, exports the client
width as `CG_LOGIN3_CLIENT_WIDTH = 69`, exports the gap as `CG_LOGIN3_PROFILE_DIVERGENCE = 3`, and
gives the 69-byte form its own named rejection `CgLogin3Error::ClientWidth`. Accepting 69 bytes
would be a Rust-only protocol that the legacy server cannot speak. This is a **legacy defect to
report against the C++ server and the client's build settings**, not something the Rust codec may
paper over.

Credentials stay raw fixed storage: `[u8; 31]` and `[u8; 17]`, with no NUL-aware accessor. The
legacy handler hands the raw pointer to the DB request, and a codec-level NUL requirement would
reject records the legacy server accepts.

### 162.4 `CgGayaSystem`: a live first-wins registration collision at header 241

This is the more serious defect, and it is invisible to any per-record audit.

`server/server/game/packet.h` assigns the same byte twice:

- line 92 — `HEADER_CG_GAYA_SYSTEM = 241`
- line 94 — `HEADER_CG_CLIENT_VERSION2 = 0xf1` (which is 241)

`server/server/game/packet_info.cpp` registers both, in this order:

- line 167 — `Set(HEADER_CG_CLIENT_VERSION2, sizeof(TPacketCGClientVersion2), "Version");`
- line 175 — `Set(HEADER_CG_GAYA_SYSTEM, sizeof(TPacketCGGayaSystem), "GayaSystemSend");`

`CPacketInfo::Set` is **first-wins**, `packet_info.cpp:18-21`:

```c
void CPacketInfo::Set(int header, int iSize, const char * c_pszName)
{
    if (m_pPacketMap.find(header) != m_pPacketMap.end())
        return;
```

So the line 175 call is a silent no-op. The framing table maps byte 241 to
`sizeof(TPacketCGClientVersion2)` = `1 + 33 + 33` = **67 bytes**.

The dispatch table is a separate `switch` and is not affected by the collision:
`server/server/game/input_main.cpp:3881` routes byte 241 to `CInputMain::GayaSystemSend`, whose
entire body is behind `#ifdef ENABLE_GAYA_SYSTEM` — and that macro **is** defined, at
`prodomodefines.h:52`. `CInputMain::GayaSystemSend` reads only `subheader` and `pos` from
`struct packet_gaya_system { BYTE header; BYTE subheader; int pos; }`, which is **6 bytes**.

The result: legacy framing hands the Gaya handler 67 bytes, the handler reads 6, and 61 bytes are
left unconsumed and re-interpreted as the next packet. `protocol/src/cg_gaya_system.rs` models
the **6-byte source record** and exposes the collision as the named constant
`CG_GAYA_SYSTEM_SHADOWED_BY = "TPacketCGClientVersion2"` with a wiring test asserting it, so the
defect is code-visible rather than buried in a comment.

### 162.5 Header 111 is shared across directions

`packet.h:77` — `HEADER_CG_LOGIN3 = 111`, a 66-byte record.
`packet.h:186` — `HEADER_GC_WALK_MODE = 111`, a 6-byte record, sent live from
`char.cpp:1219`, `char.cpp:1232`, and `char.cpp:7364`.

The two directions are framed by different tables, so this is **not** a collision. It is recorded
here because a name-based or direction-blind header audit will report it as one. Direction is
load-bearing for every header byte in both enums.

### 162.6 Feature profiles chosen for the remaining records

- **`CgRefine`, 3 bytes.** `BYTE pos; BYTE type;`. The alternative `WORD pos` shape in the source
  is commented out and is dead text, not a feature profile.
- **`Attr67AddData`, 6 bytes**, `WORD, BYTE, WORD, BYTE`. The four fields already sum to six and
  the natural alignment is two, so `#pragma pack(1)` changes nothing and no explicit packing
  discussion is needed. `CgAttr67Add` is 8 bytes: header, an opaque subheader byte, then the
  nested six.
- **`CgExchange`, 14 bytes** — the active `ENABLE_REMOVE_LIMIT_GOLD` profile is
  `header, subheader, DWORD, BYTE, TItemPos` = 10, and the active profile is
  `header, subheader, QWORD, BYTE, TItemPos` = 14. The inactive width is recorded as
  `CG_EXCHANGE_DWORD_PROFILE_SIZE = 10` with a test pinning the four-byte difference.
- **`CgAnswerMakeGuild`, 14 bytes** — header plus a raw 13-byte guild name. No NUL requirement:
  the legacy field is `char[13]` and a name shorter than 13 bytes is accepted verbatim.
- **`CgHack`, 257 bytes** — header plus a raw `[u8; 256]`. Not UTF-8, not NUL-terminated. The
  login phase consumes and drops it (`case HEADER_CG_HACK: break;`); the main and dead phases both
  log it and close the character.
- **`CgChangeLook`, 10 bytes** — `header, subheader, DWORD dwCost, BYTE bPos, TItemPos tPos`, with
  `__CHANGELOOK_SYSTEM__` active at `prodomodefines.h:16`. `bPos` and `tPos` are **not** two views
  of one field. `tPos` is the shared packed 3-byte `ItemPos`; this is its fourth consumer after
  `cg_sash`, `cg_dragon_soul`, and `cg_exchange`.
- **`CgCubeRenewal`, 14 bytes** — `header, subheader, DWORD index_item, DWORD count_item, DWORD
  index_item_improve`.
- **`CgFlyTarget`, 13 bytes** — one body, two headers, `HEADER_CG_FLY_TARGETING = 0x33` and
  `HEADER_CG_ADD_FLY_TARGETING = 0x35`. The 12-byte bodies are identical, so the header is the
  only thing that distinguishes the two actions. `CgFlyTargetHeader` is an explicit required
  argument to `new`; there is no default variant, and a wiring test asserts the two encodings
  differ in exactly one byte.
- **`CgOnClick` / `CgTargetInfoLoad`, 5 bytes** — opaque `u32` VIDs. Existence and authorisation are
  runtime and session policy, not framing.
- **The seven `u8` argument records** — `ChangeLanguage`, `RequestEventData`, `PremiumPlayers`,
  `RefineElement`, `WorldBoss`, `DailyGift`, `Biologist`. All 256 values round-trip. Handler
  switch statements, sentinels, and range checks are **not** framing constraints. `CG_REFINE_ELEMENT_CLOSE
  = 255` is exported as a semantic constant for handler code to compare against, never as a
  validation rule. `ChangeLanguage` keeps its server/client registration divergence (238 vs 245)
  documented and its value opaque.
- **`CgText` and `CgEnvanterBlack`, 1 byte each.** `CgText` is registered but neither dispatched
  nor sent anywhere in the server; it receives a codec because registration is real. `ENVANTER_BLACK
  = 226` is a keepalive byte consumed by the input loop before the header map lookup, so it is the
  one header in this section with **no** `HEADER_CG_`-prefixed constant; it is exported as
  `ENVANTER_BLACK` and a wiring test records that asymmetry deliberately.

### 162.7 `HEADER_CG_KEY_AGREEMENT` is not pending work

The final unimplemented row is `HEADER_CG_KEY_AGREEMENT = 0xfb`, 261 bytes, registered `Conditional`.
Both halves of that record are behind a macro that is never defined:

- `server/server/game/packet_info.cpp:190-192` — the `Set()` call is inside
  `#ifdef _IMPROVED_PACKET_ENCRYPTION_`
- `server/server/game/packet.h:2721-2737` — `struct TPacketKeyAgreement` and
  `TPacketKeyAgreementCompleted` are inside the same `#ifdef`

Across the entire `server/` and `client/` trees there is exactly one `#define
_IMPROVED_PACKET_ENCRYPTION_`, at `client/Client/EterBase/ServiceDefs.h:4`, and it is
**commented out**:

```c
// #define _IMPROVED_PACKET_ENCRYPTION_
```

So the improved DH2 key-exchange path is compiled out on both sides. The CG inventory is
therefore **complete for the active build**: 92 rows, 91 implemented, 1 dead. Implementing the
record would add a codec for bytes the checked-in server can never receive.

## 163. GAME-TO-CLIENT AND GAME-TO-GAME COVERAGE: HONEST BASELINE

Sections 152 through 162 closed the client-to-game (CG) direction. This section
establishes the honest baseline for the two remaining client-visible and
peer directions before any new codec is written, and corrects three method
defects that had produced wrong answers earlier in the rewrite.

### 163.1 A `--include=*.h` search bug invalidated earlier client feature-macro results

Every client-side search in this rewrite used `grep --include=*.h`. That glob is
case-sensitive, and the client's most important feature header is
`client/Client/UserInterface/LOCALE_INC.H` with an uppercase extension. Only two
uppercase-extension headers exist in the whole tree
(`client/Extern/include/MSS.H` and `LOCALE_INC.H`), and one of them is the single
file that defines the client's feature switches.

The consequence was a false negative. A recursive search for
`^#\s*define\s+ENABLE_SASH_SYSTEM` reported "no definition found in client
headers", and a follow-up search reported the same for `ENABLE_AURA_SYSTEM`,
`ENABLE_CONQUEROR_LEVEL`, and `ENABLE_GAYA_SYSTEM`. All four are in fact defined
in `LOCALE_INC.H`, at lines 25, 84, 89, and 94 respectively.

Verified reproductions:

```text
# both return rc=1 with no output
grep -RnIE --include=*.h -e '^\s*#\s*define\s+ENABLE_GAYA_SYSTEM\b' /workspace/client/Client
grep -RnIE --include=*.H -e '^\s*#\s*define\s+ENABLE_GAYA_SYSTEM\b' /workspace/client/Client
# returns a match
grep -RnIE -e '^\s*#\s*define\s+ENABLE_GAYA_SYSTEM\b' /workspace/client/Client
```

Rules adopted for the rest of the rewrite:

- Never pass `--include=*.h` when auditing this tree. Either omit `--include`
  and filter in code, or pass both `*.h` and `*.H`.
- Every negative search result must be accompanied by a positive control on the
  same pattern over the same tree, and a named negative control.
- Prefer reading files in code with `Path.read_text(errors="replace")` over
  shelling out to `grep`, so that extension case cannot silently drop a file.
  Legacy and client files in this repository contain non-UTF-8 bytes.

The server tree was not affected: its feature header is
`server/server/common/prodomodefines.h`, all lowercase.

### 163.2 The client feature-macro set is defined in `LOCALE_INC.H`

`LOCALE_INC.H` contributes 131 empty-or-numeric `#define`s. The ones that gate
protocol records include `ENABLE_MULTI_LANGUAGE_SYSTEM` (line 110),
`ENABLE_SASH_SYSTEM` (25), `ENABLE_AURA_SYSTEM` (84), `ENABLE_CONQUEROR_LEVEL`
(89), `ENABLE_GAYA_SYSTEM` (94), `ENABLE_REFINE_ELEMENT` (87),
`ENABLE_CHANGELOOK_SYSTEM`, `ENABLE_FISH_EVENT`, `ENABLE_MESSENGER_TEAM`,
`ENABLE_SWITCHBOT`, `ENABLE_REWARD_SYSTEM`, and `__ENABLE_SHAMAN_SYSTEM__`.
`ENABLE_DICE_SYSTEM`, `ENABLE_GROWTH_PET_SYSTEM`,
`ENABLE_PRIVATE_SHOP_APPLY_RANDOM`, `ENABLE_PRIVATE_SHOP_CHANGE_LOOK`, and
`ENABLE_PRIVATE_SHOP_REFINE_ELEMENT` are not defined.

The checked-in client Visual Studio project files set no `ENABLE_*` or `__*`
macro at all. The only client project preprocessor definitions found are
`WIN32`, `_CRT_SECURE_NO_WARNINGS`, `WINDOWS_IGNORE_PACKING_MISMATCH`,
`_WINDOWS`, `USE_LOD`, `DUNGEON_WORK`, `_DEBUG`, and `NDEBUG`. The client
feature set therefore comes entirely from `LOCALE_INC.H`.

Two consequences:

- `CHR_EQUIPPART_NUM` is 6 in both trees, not 4. The client's
  `ECharacterEquipmentPart` enum adds `CHR_EQUIPPART_SASH` under
  `ENABLE_SASH_SYSTEM` and `CHR_EQUIPPART_AURA` under `ENABLE_AURA_SYSTEM`, and
  both are defined. The server's equivalent enum uses `__SASH_SYSTEM__` and
  `__AURA_SYSTEM__`, both also defined in `prodomodefines.h`. The trees agree.
  The two trees do use different macro spellings for the same features, so a
  macro name must never be assumed to transfer between them.

### 163.3 Correction: `TPacketCGLogin3` is an unconditional 3-byte mismatch

Section 162 recorded the `LOGIN3` divergence as conditional, on the grounds that
the client macro `ENABLE_MULTI_LANGUAGE_SYSTEM` was not found in the tree and
appeared to be a Visual Studio project setting. That was wrong, and it was wrong
because of the `--include=*.h` bug in 163.1. The macro is defined at
`client/Client/UserInterface/LOCALE_INC.H:110`.

The divergence is therefore unconditional in both checked-in trees:

| side | macro | definition | language field | width |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| server `packet.h:480-489` | `__MULTI_LANGUAGE_SYSTEM__` | `prodomodefines.h:133` | `BYTE bLanguage` | 66 |
| client `Packet.h:436-445` | `ENABLE_MULTI_LANGUAGE_SYSTEM` | `LOCALE_INC.H:110` | `DWORD bLanguage` | 69 |

`packet_info.cpp:109` registers header 111 at 66 bytes. The three-byte
difference desynchronizes framing. `protocol::cg_login3` already models the
server's 66-byte profile as the active one and rejects the 69-byte client shape
as `CgLogin3Error::ClientWidth`; that behaviour is correct and is no longer
conditional. This is a genuine server/client protocol defect in the checked-in
sources, not a build-configuration question.

### 163.4 The game-to-client registration table lives in the client, not the server

`server/server/game/packet_info.cpp` registers 129 entries: 92 client-to-game,
36 game-to-game, and one `ENVANTER_BLACK`. It registers no game-to-client
records, because that table is the inbound side of the game server's input loop.
Game-to-client coverage cannot be measured from it.

The authoritative game-to-client framing table is the client's
`CNetworkPacketHeaderMap`, populated in
`client/Client/UserInterface/PythonNetworkStream.cpp` by 134 `Set` calls:
115 `STATIC_SIZE_PACKET` and 19 `DYNAMIC_SIZE_PACKET` registrations covering 127
distinct packed structs. All 134 header bytes are distinct, so the table has no
first-wins or last-wins ambiguity in practice.

Note that the client's `CNetworkPacketHeaderMap::Set` is last-wins
(`m_headerMap[header] = rPacketType`), the opposite of the game server's
`CPacketInfo::Set`, which returns early when the byte is already present. The
two policies only differ if a byte is registered twice, which does not happen in
this table.

### 163.5 The four cross-tree `HEADER_GC_*` value differences are naming inversions

A name-keyed comparison of the client and server `HEADER_GC_*` enums reports
four names with different byte values:

| name | server | client |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `HEADER_GC_SKILL_LEVEL` | 76 | 72 |
| `HEADER_GC_MAIN_CHARACTER` | 113 | 15 |
| `HEADER_GC_REFINE_INFORMATION` | 119 | 95 |
| `HEADER_GC_ITEM_SET` | 21 | 20 |

A full audit of all four, covering send sites, client registrations, client
handler dispatch, and a field-by-field layout comparison under `pack(1)`, found
that **none is a wire incompatibility**. Each is the same record generation
under two different names, because the two trees renamed in opposite
directions. The server suffixes the legacy generation with `_OLD`; the client
suffixes the modern generation with `_NEW` or a numeric suffix.

| server name (byte) | matching client name (byte) | width | layout |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `HEADER_GC_SKILL_LEVEL` (76) | `HEADER_GC_SKILL_LEVEL_NEW` (76) | 1531 | identical |
| `HEADER_GC_MAIN_CHARACTER` (113) | `HEADER_GC_MAIN_CHARACTER2_EMPIRE` (113) | 46 | identical |
| `HEADER_GC_REFINE_INFORMATION` (119) | `HEADER_GC_REFINE_INFORMATION_NEW` (119) | 60 | identical |
| `HEADER_GC_ITEM_SET` (21) | `HEADER_GC_ITEM_SET2` (21) | 72 | identical |

Supporting evidence:

- The server never sends its own 72, 15, or 95 constants. A search for
  `HEADER_GC_*_OLD` assignments in the server tree returns nothing, and the
  three `_OLD` enumerators have no struct and no send site.
- Each of the four has exactly one send site, none behind a disabled `#ifdef`:
  `char_skill.cpp:178`, `char.cpp:2018`, `char_item.cpp:1891`, and
  `char_item.cpp:572`.
- The client registers and handles both generations in all four cases.
- The client's own debug name table in `EterLib/NetStream.cpp` uses a third
  vocabulary, naming byte 76 `HEADER_GC_SKILL_LEVEL_NEW` and byte 113
  `HEADER_GC_MAIN_CHARACTER_NEW`.

The generalizable rule, now encoded in `protocol::gc_inventory`: **a name-keyed
enum diff across these two trees is unsound.** Header tables must be paired by
byte value, and every value must be checked in both trees.

Value-keyed pairing over the full 134-row table resolves 20 client names that
differ from the server name for the same byte, including the four above. Five
client registrations have no server enumerator at all:
`HEADER_GC_SKILL_COOLTIME_END` (73), `HEADER_GC_CHARACTER_ADD2` (120),
`HEADER_GC_CHARACTER_UPDATE2` (117), `HEADER_GC_SAFEBOX_MONEY_CHANGE` (84), and
`HEADER_GC_UNK_213` (213).

### 163.6 Game-to-client coverage is 14 of 134, and the metric must be keyed by byte

Measured with whole-token matching over the comment-stripped text of
`protocol/src/*.rs`, game-to-client coverage is **14 of 134 registered records
(10 percent), leaving 120 records with no codec.**

Getting this number right required correcting two wrong answers in sequence, and
both corrections are the same lesson.

A substring metric reports 13 implemented, because `HEADER_GC_CHARACTER_DEL`
and `HEADER_GC_TIME` are counted by matching inside the longer names
`HEADER_GC_CHARACTER_DELETE_SUCCESS` and `HEADER_GC_TIME_SYNC`. That is the
substring-metric failure already recorded for CG in Section 162, now reproduced
in a second direction.

A whole-token metric keyed on the **client-side** name then reports 11, and
that is still wrong, for the same reason section 163.5 documents: the two trees
rename record generations in opposite directions. Three implemented records are
coded under their **server** name, so a client-name scan cannot see them.

| byte | client name | server name | Rust constant |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6 | `HEADER_GC_LOGIN_SUCCESS3` | `HEADER_GC_LOGIN_SUCCESS` | `HEADER_GC_LOGIN_SUCCESS` |
| 32 | `HEADER_GC_LOGIN_SUCCESS4` | `HEADER_GC_LOGIN_SUCCESS_NEWSLOT` | `HEADER_GC_LOGIN_SUCCESS_NEWSLOT` |
| 252 | `HEADER_GC_HANDSHAKE_OK` | `HEADER_GC_TIME_SYNC` | `HEADER_GC_TIME_SYNC` |

The correct metric resolves every `HEADER_GC_*` enumerator the crate declares,
looks each one's value up in the legacy tables, and marks the **rows for those
bytes**. `protocol::gc_inventory` stores that flag per row, and the test
`implementation_status_is_keyed_by_wire_byte_not_by_client_name` fails if the
three renamed rows are ever reverted to `false`.

The rule generalizes: **never key a coverage or implementation metric on a
protocol identifier name.** Legacy header tables here are two vocabularies for
one set of wire bytes. Key on the byte.

The fourteen implemented records are every early-phase login or handshake
record: bytes 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 32, 44, 118, 150, 252, 253, 254, and 255.
Nothing in the game phase, the movement, item, party, guild, messenger, shop,
or quest directions is implemented.

The honest summary of protocol coverage is therefore:

| direction | registered | implemented | missing |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| client to game | 92 | 91 | 1 (dead) |
| game to client | 134 | 14 | 120 |
| game to game | 36 | 4 | 32 |

The remaining protocol work is 152 records, not 1. Any statement that the
protocol layer is complete is false.

### 163.7 A packed-width calculator is correct only for simple records

To size the game-to-client backlog, a `#pragma pack(1)` width calculator was
built that evaluates each header's real `#ifdef` gates against a macro set
collected from the same tree, and extracts only top-level struct members so that
C++ classes with inline method bodies are handled.

Validated against eight independently hand-summed ground-truth widths, it
matched three and failed five. Every failure traced to constant resolution, not
to the field walk: the calculator resolved `ITEM_ATTRIBUTE_MAX_NUM` to 4 when
the real active value is 7, because the constant is an alias
(`= ITEM_ATTRIBUTE_RARE_END`) whose value requires a second-order enum
resolution that the tool does not perform. Under-resolving that constant
under-counted `TPacketGCItemSet` as 63 bytes against a true 72.

The width calculator is therefore **not** used to publish widths.
`protocol::gc_inventory` deliberately has no size column. Game-to-client widths
are heavily feature gated, and an automated width that is silently wrong is
worse than an absent one. Widths belong in the individual codec modules, where
each is hand-summed against the struct source and cited, which is how the
game-to-game table in 163.8 was produced.

### 163.8 Game-to-game coverage is 4 of 36, and the DB server needs no GG codec

The legacy game-to-game table has 36 `Set` registrations. Whole-token coverage
in the `protocol` crate is 4: `HEADER_GG_SETUP`,
`HEADER_GG_FIND_POSITION`, `HEADER_GG_WARP_CHARACTER`, and
`HEADER_GG_GUILD_WAR_ZONE_MAP_INDEX`. **32 records have no codec.**

Framing, from `game/input.cpp:58-124` and `input_p2p.cpp:31-33`: the shared
`CInputProcessor` reads one header byte, looks the total length up in the bound
table, and closes the descriptor on an unknown header. The game-to-game wire
shape is therefore `[u8 header][body]`, with no length prefix, no handle, and
no padding. Header byte zero is a one-byte special case. This is a different
socket and a different shape from the DB peer's `[u8 header][u32 handle][u32
size]`, so the two lookup tables must never be shared.

The DB server consumes **no** game-to-game record. Searches over
`server/server/db` find no `HEADER_GG_` enumerator, no `TPacketGG` type, no
`CPacketInfoGG`, and no inclusion of the game packet header at all; positive
controls on the same patterns return 15 and 4 files for `HEADER_DG_` and
`HEADER_GD_`. The DB's only peer-to-peer involvement is relaying a port number
in a DG frame. **The Rust `db-server` needs no GG decoder for any of the 32.**

The 32 unimplemented records fall into three groups by porting cost:

- **Fixed width, scalar members only (20 records).** `HEADER_GG_LOGOUT` (26),
  `HEADER_GG_SHUTDOWN` (1), `HEADER_GG_DISCONNECT` (32), `HEADER_GG_SHOUT`
  (515), `HEADER_GG_MESSENGER_ADD` and `HEADER_GG_MESSENGER_REMOVE` (51 each,
  one shared body), `HEADER_GG_TRANSFER` (34), `HEADER_GG_XMAS_WARP_SANTA` (6),
  `HEADER_GG_XMAS_WARP_SANTA_REPLY` (2), `HEADER_GG_RELOAD_CRC_LIST` (1, no
  struct and no producer), `HEADER_GG_LOGIN_PING` (32),
  `HEADER_GG_CHECK_CLIENT_VERSION` (1, no struct and no producer),
  `HEADER_GG_BLOCK_CHAT` (34), `HEADER_GG_SIEGE` (3),
  `HEADER_GG_MONARCH_TRANSFER` (13), `HEADER_GG_CHECK_AWAKENESS` (1, never
  written), `HEADER_GG_EVENT_RELOAD` (1), `HEADER_GG_EVENT_HIDE_AND_SEEK` (9),
  `HEADER_GG_REWARD_INFO` (2), `HEADER_GG_MULTI_FARM` (57),
  `HEADER_GG_LOCALE_NOTICE` (3080),
  `HEADER_GG_PRIVATE_SHOP_ITEM_SEARCH_UPDATE` (10).
- **Contains a nested struct (3 records).** `HEADER_GG_SWITCHBOT` (187, nested
  three levels deep and pulling in the typed item-attribute record),
  `HEADER_GG_EVENT` (87, whose nested `TEventTable` is also the DB boot event
  payload element and can be shared), `HEADER_GG_PRIVATE_SHOP_ITEM_SEARCH` (94,
  whose client-to-game twin has a different field order and must not be merged).
- **Variable length, prefix plus a self-described tail (5 records).**
  `HEADER_GG_RELAY` (30-byte prefix plus a 32-bit `lSize`),
  `HEADER_GG_NOTICE` (5-byte prefix plus a 32-bit `lSize` whose tail includes
  the NUL), `HEADER_GG_MONARCH_NOTICE` (6-byte prefix plus a 32-bit `lSize`),
  `HEADER_GG_GUILD` (6-byte prefix, tail chosen by `bSubHeader`),
  `HEADER_GG_PRIVATE_SHOP_ITEM_SEARCH_RESULT` (7-byte prefix plus a **16-bit**
  `wSize`).

For these five, the registered size is a minimum, not a frame length, because
the legacy `Analyze` step returns a non-zero extra length that the input
processor adds to the table length.

`HEADER_GG_GUILD` is the hardest record in the family: a sub-header switch where
sub-header 0 appends a 519-byte nested guild-chat record, sub-header 1 appends a
bare 4-byte `int` with no struct at all, and any other value logs an error and
ends the frame at 6 bytes.

`HEADER_GG_MULTI_FARM` carries a dead wire field: its `size` member is never
written by any producer and never read by the handler. The four bytes must still
be preserved, exactly as the dead count byte in `CgItemGive` is.

### 163.9 Game-to-game records that are dead, unused, or unregistered

- `HEADER_GG_BIG_NOTICE` (30) is dead end to end. Its enumerator
  (`packet.h:257-259`), its registration (`packet_info.cpp:238-240`), its
  dispatch case (`input_p2p.cpp:588-593`), its GM producer, and its three Lua
  bindings are all behind `ENABLE_FULL_NOTICE`, which is defined nowhere in the
  server or client trees. `protocol::gg_inventory` documents it but
  deliberately makes it non-resolving. Like `HEADER_CG_KEY_AGREEMENT`, it is
  not backlog work.
- `TPacketGGForkedMapInfo` (`packet.h:321-328`, 3 bytes) is declared but never
  used, and is not registered, so its 3-byte form is unreachable on the wire.
  Both the typedef and the struct-tag spellings were swept.
- `HEADER_GG_BLOCK_EXCEPTION` (24) is the one game-to-game enumerator with no
  struct, no registration, and no dispatch case.
- `TPacketGGShutdown` is 1 byte, `HEADER_GG_CHECK_AWAKENESS` is 1 byte, and both
  `HEADER_GG_RELOAD_CRC_LIST` and `HEADER_GG_CHECK_CLIENT_VERSION` are
  registered as `sizeof(BYTE)` with handlers that never dereference the body.
  For all four the single header byte is the whole frame.

The client never sees any game-to-game record: no `HEADER_GG_` token appears
anywhere in the client tree, against many `HEADER_GC_` hits. Game-to-game is
purely server-to-server, so there is no client-side collision to check.

### 163.10 New modules, gates, and what this section does not claim

Added in this section:

- `protocol/src/gc_inventory.rs`, 1586 lines. `GcHeader`, `GcFraming`,
  `LegacyGcPacket`, `LEGACY_GC_PACKET_INVENTORY` with all 134 rows, and
  `resolve_gc_packet` and `gc_missing_codec_count`. Ten unit tests. Each row
  pairs the client registration name with the server enumerator name for the
  same wire byte, and records framing and implementation status.
- `protocol/src/gg_inventory.rs`, 666 lines. `GgHeader`, `GgRecordShape`,
  `LegacyGgPacket`, `LEGACY_GG_PACKET_INVENTORY` with all 36 rows,
  `resolve_gg_packet`, and `resolve_gg_base_size`. Nine unit tests. Every width
  is hand-summed and source-verified.
- Both modules are registered in `protocol/src/lib.rs`.

The strict gate receipts for this section are recorded in 163.11.

This section does not claim any game-to-client or game-to-game record is
implemented beyond the eleven and four already listed. It does not claim the
protocol layer is complete. It establishes the baseline so that the next
implementation batches can be measured honestly.

## 164. THE SMALL FIXED-WIDTH GAME-TO-CLIENT RECORDS

Section 163 measured the game-to-client backlog at 120 records. This section
implements the eighteen smallest of them plus a correction to the metric itself.

### 164.1 Correcting the coverage metric to 14, then to 32

Section 163.6 recorded 11 implemented game-to-client records. That number was
wrong, and fixing it exposed a rule that applies to every metric in this
rewrite.

The Rust codecs declare their header constants using the **server** names.
Three implemented records are therefore invisible to any scan keyed on the
**client** name:

| byte | client name | server name | Rust constant |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6 | `HEADER_GC_LOGIN_SUCCESS3` | `HEADER_GC_LOGIN_SUCCESS` | `HEADER_GC_LOGIN_SUCCESS` |
| 32 | `HEADER_GC_LOGIN_SUCCESS4` | `HEADER_GC_LOGIN_SUCCESS_NEWSLOT` | `HEADER_GC_LOGIN_SUCCESS_NEWSLOT` |
| 252 | `HEADER_GC_HANDSHAKE_OK` | `HEADER_GC_TIME_SYNC` | `HEADER_GC_TIME_SYNC` |

This is the same naming inversion documented in 163.5, and it has now produced
two wrong counts in a row: first a substring scan over-counted, then a
client-name scan under-counted. The correct procedure is to resolve every
`HEADER_GC_*` enumerator the crate declares, look up each one's numeric value in
the legacy tables, and mark the rows for **those bytes**.

`protocol::gc_inventory` now stores implementation status per byte value, and
the test `implementation_status_is_keyed_by_wire_byte_not_by_client_name` fails
if any of the three renamed rows is ever reverted. The corrected baseline was
**14 of 134**.

### 164.2 The new module

`protocol/src/gc_small.rs` implements 18 records. All are `#pragma pack(1)`
structures of one to four bytes whose body is a single opaque `BYTE`.

| byte | record | packed width | server producer |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 28 | `HEADER_GC_QUICKSLOT_ADD` | 4 | `char_quickslot.cpp:90-94` |
| 29 | `HEADER_GC_QUICKSLOT_DEL` | 2 | `char_quickslot.cpp:109-112` |
| 30 | `HEADER_GC_QUICKSLOT_SWAP` | 3 | `char_quickslot.cpp:130-134` |
| 73 | `HEADER_GC_SKILL_COOLTIME_END` | 2 | **none** |
| 82 | `HEADER_GC_REQUEST_MAKE_GUILD` | 1 | `questlua_game.cpp:57-58` |
| 83 | `HEADER_GC_PARTY_PARAMETER` | 2 | `party.cpp:1595` |
| 87 | `HEADER_GC_SAFEBOX_WRONG_PASSWORD` | 1 | `input_db.cpp:1174-1176` |
| 88 | `HEADER_GC_SAFEBOX_SIZE` | 2 | `char.cpp:7120-7125`, `char.cpp:7166-7171` |
| 90 | `HEADER_GC_EMPIRE` | 2 | `input_db.cpp:164,172,1254` |
| 112 | `HEADER_GC_CHANGE_SKILL_GROUP` | 2 | **none** |
| 121 | `HEADER_GC_CHANNEL` | 2 | `input_login.cpp:691` |
| 122 | `HEADER_GC_MALL_OPEN` | 2 | `char.cpp:7230-7235` |
| 132 | `HEADER_GC_LOVE_POINT_UPDATE` | 2 | `marriage.cpp:351` |

| 212 | `HEADER_GC_DS_PLUS_CHANGE_ATTR_RESULT` | 2 | `char.cpp:11248` |
| 213 | `HEADER_GC_UNK_213` | 2 | **none** |
| 245 | `HEADER_GC_REQUEST_CHANGE_LANGUAGE` | 2 | `char.cpp:11637` |

Each width was hand-summed from the struct source in both trees and is not the
output of the rejected width calculator from 163.7. The module holds 29 unit
tests, and six public-API wiring tests were added to
`protocol/tests/cg_wiring.rs`, which grew from 36 to 42.

### 164.3 Three legacy hazards the module makes explicit

**The server reuses `CG`-prefixed struct names for outbound records.**
`TPacketCGSafeboxSize` carries both `HEADER_GC_SAFEBOX_SIZE` and
`HEADER_GC_MALL_OPEN`, and `TPacketCGSafeboxWrongPassword` carries
`HEADER_GC_SAFEBOX_WRONG_PASSWORD`. Both live in `server/server/game/packet.h`
and both are sent from `char.cpp` and `input_db.cpp`. Searching the server tree
for `TPacketGC*` misses them, which is how they ended up looking client-only in
an earlier pass. The module documents the `CG`-prefixed names in the
`GcHeaderAndByte` type documentation.

**Field names differ while the wire does not.**
`TPacketGCQuickSlotSwap` is `{ header; pos; change_pos; }` on the client and
`{ header; pos; pos_to; }` on the server. Same order, same three `BYTE`s. The
test `quick_slot_swap_keeps_the_client_field_names_over_the_server_spelling`
pins the third wire byte so a rename cannot silently drop it.

**Three client-decoded records have no server producer at all.** A whole-token
search over `server/server` returns zero hits for
`HEADER_GC_SKILL_COOLTIME_END`, `HEADER_GC_CHANGE_SKILL_GROUP`, and
`HEADER_GC_UNK_213`; the server has no enumerator for bytes 73, 112, or 213.
Byte 73 is the starkest case: the client registers it, names it, and has no
dispatch case for it at all. These are still real client decode entries, so their
framing is real and the module implements them, but they are unreachable in the
checked-in server.

### 164.4 One C++ `bool` kept as a raw byte

`TPacketGCDragonSoulChangeAttrResult` is `{ BYTE header; bool result; }` in
`server/server/game/packet.h`. Under `#pragma pack(1)` the `bool` occupies one
byte, so the packed width is 2. The body is stored as a raw `u8`, not a Rust
`bool`, because the wire carries whatever byte the sender wrote and a `bool`
would collapse every non-zero value to `true`. The test
`the_dragon_soul_result_keeps_a_non_boolean_byte_raw` round-trips all 256 values.

This is the same rule already applied to dead wire fields elsewhere in the
rewrite, and it is the reason the module has no `bool` anywhere.

### 164.5 Two shared shapes instead of ten near-duplicate types

Nine of the records are structurally identical: a header byte and one opaque
body byte, with a different field name in each legacy struct. They are modelled
as one `GcHeaderAndByte` with a caller-supplied header, plus two dedicated types
where the client-only semantics justify them (`GcSkillCoolTimeEnd`,
`GcDragonSoulChangeAttrResult`, `GcUnk213`).

This is not a lossy merge. The header is the only thing separating the records
on the wire, the body byte is opaque in all nine cases, and inventing nine
near-identical Rust structs would imply nine distinct legacy structs that do not
exist. `GcQuickSlotAdd` keeps its own type because it nests the shared 2-byte
`GcQuickSlot` body and is therefore 4 bytes.

The test `the_nine_header_and_byte_game_to_client_records_agree_with_the_inventory`
asserts that all twelve two-byte headers are distinct, which is the property that
makes one shared shape safe.

### 164.6 Updated coverage and the remaining backlog

| direction | registered | implemented | missing |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| client to game | 92 | 91 | 1 (dead) |
| game to game | 36 | 4 | 32 |
| game to client | 134 | 32 | 102 |

Game-to-client coverage is now 24 percent. Every record implemented so far is
still an early-phase login, handshake, or single-byte notification; nothing in
the movement, item, party, guild, messenger, shop, quest, or skill directions
has a codec.

The next batch is the small fixed-width records that carry a `DWORD` or a short
`char` array, which need a real field walk rather than an opaque byte. The
`HEADER_GC_UNK_213` row and the two other producer-less records should be treated
as reachability questions for the server rather than as porting work.

## 165. THE GAME-TO-CLIENT RECORDS THAT CARRY ONE 32-BIT VALUE

### 165.1 What this batch covers

`protocol/src/gc_vid.rs` implements 20 game-to-client records of 5 to 7 packed
bytes. It is the second game-to-client batch after section 164's 18 records.

| wire shape | width | records | byte values |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| header + `DWORD` | 5 | 11 | 2, 13, 14, 27, 77, 80, 84, 86, 106, 124, 129 |
| header + `DWORD` + `BYTE` | 6 | 3 | 43, 111, 127 |
| header + `BYTE` + `DWORD` | 6 | 1 | 114 |
| header + `WORD` + `WORD` + `BYTE` | 6 | 1 | 228 |
| header + `DWORD` + `WORD` | 7 | 1 | 18 |
| header + `WORD[3]` | 7 | 1 | 157 |
| header + subheader + `DWORD` + `BYTE` | 7 | 1 | 89 |
| header + `BYTE` + `ItemPos` | 5 | 1 | 209 |

The module holds 33 unit tests, and seven public wiring tests were added to
`protocol/tests/cg_wiring.rs`, which grew from 42 to 49.

### 165.2 Three field types whose width depends on the legacy target

`server/server/premake5.lua:12` sets `architecture "x86"`, so the legacy server
and client are 32-bit. That is not a detail here: it fixes the width of three
non-fixed-width field types used by these records.

- C++ `long` is 4 bytes. `HEADER_GC_TARGET_DELETE` (124) is
  `{ BYTE bHeader; long lID; }`, so it is 5 bytes rather than 9.
- `time_t` is 4 bytes. `HEADER_GC_TIME` (106) is
  `{ BYTE bHeader; time_t time; }`, so it is 5 bytes. No `_TIME_BITS=64`
  definition exists anywhere in the tree. This confirms the 5-byte `GC_TIME`
  width recorded in section 162.
- A C++ `bool` is 1 byte, handled in section 164.

A 64-bit reading of any of these three would silently break the framing, so the
`x86` setting is cited in the module documentation rather than assumed.

### 165.3 A feature profile that resolves through the uppercase-extension header

`TPacketGCItemDel`, which carries both `HEADER_GC_SAFEBOX_DEL` (86) and
`HEADER_GC_MALL_DEL` (129), is written

```c
BYTE header;
#if defined(__EXTENDED_SAFEBOX__)
    DWORD pos;
#else
    BYTE pos;
#endif
```

in both `client/Client/UserInterface/Packet.h:1796-1801` and
`server/server/game/packet.h:1447-1452`. The macro is defined on both sides, at
`server/server/common/prodomodefines.h:61` and
`client/Client/UserInterface/LOCALE_INC.H:35`, so the active record is the
5-byte `DWORD` form. The 2-byte form is unreachable and is not implemented.

This is a direct, concrete consequence of the `--include=*.h` defect in section
163.1. `LOCALE_INC.H` has an uppercase extension, so the macro appears
undefined to a `*.h` search, and the record looks 2 bytes instead of 5. A whole
token search over both extensions, plus a positive control, resolves it.

### 165.4 One struct, two headers, sent from a single ternary

`HEADER_GC_SAFEBOX_DEL` (86) and `HEADER_GC_MALL_DEL` (129) are the same
`TPacketGCItemDel`. The only place the server sends either is
`server/server/game/safebox.cpp:117-122`:

```c
TPacketGCItemDel pack;
pack.header = m_bWindowMode == SAFEBOX ? HEADER_GC_SAFEBOX_DEL : HEADER_GC_MALL_DEL;
pack.pos    = dwPos;
m_pkChrOwner->GetDesc()->Packet(&pack, sizeof(pack));
```

One struct, one send site, two header bytes. The header is the only thing
separating the records, which is the same situation as
`HEADER_CG_FLY_TARGETING` in section 161. Both bytes are implemented and the
test `safebox_del_and_mall_del_share_a_struct_but_not_a_header` pins that the
two wire bytes stay distinct.

### 165.5 A shared field that has two meanings

`HEADER_GC_FISHING` (89) is
`{ BYTE header; BYTE subheader; DWORD info; BYTE dir; }`, packed width 7 for
**every** sub-header, so the frame length does not depend on the sub-header.

`info` is not one thing. The server writes the character's `GetVID()` for
`START`, `STOP`, `REACT`, `SUCCESS`, and `FAIL` (`fishing.cpp:406-428`), but for
`FISH` it writes the fish item's vnum (`fishing.cpp:501-503`). The client
branches on the sub-header before reading it
(`PythonNetworkStreamPhaseGame.cpp:4399-4401,4434`).

The module therefore models `GcFishingSubheader` as a typed enum with an
explicit `Unknown(u8)` arm, keeps `info` as a raw `u32`, and exposes two named
accessors, `actor_vid()` and `fish_vnum()`, that return `None` for the
sub-header where the reading is wrong. That keeps the ambiguity visible instead
of hiding it behind a field name that is wrong half the time.

`FISHING_SUBHEADER_GC_*` is an anonymous enum that auto-increments from zero in
both trees in the same order, so `START` through `FISH` are 0 through 5. The
module does not invent a `default` arm: the client's `switch` has none, so an
undefined sub-header is consumed and ignored rather than rejected, and
`Unknown` preserves that.

`dir` is a `u8`, not an `i8`. The client computes `float(dir) * 5.0f`, and
reinterpreting the same byte as a signed value would change the sign of 128
through 255.

### 165.6 A C++ class that is not a struct

`SPacketGCDragonSoulRefine` (byte 209) is a C++ **class** with a user-supplied
constructor, not a plain `typedef struct`:

```cpp
class SPacketGCDragonSoulRefine
{
public:
    SPacketGCDragonSoulRefine() : header(HEADER_GC_DRAGON_SOUL_REFINE) {}
    BYTE header;
    BYTE bSubType;
    TItemPos Pos;
};
```

The constructor only initialises `header`. There is no base class and no virtual
member, so the packed layout is 1 + 1 + 3 = 5 and `TItemPos` gives this record
its fourth consumer in the crate, after `cg_sash`, `cg_dragon_soul`, and
`cg_change_look`. A struct-body extractor that only understood the
`} NAME;` typedef form would have missed the server's `struct packet_position`
and this class entirely, which is why the extractor in this section handles
both `} NAME;` and `struct NAME { ... };`.

### 165.7 Four shapes that would be identical in length but wrong in order

Four of these records are 6 or 7 bytes with different field layouts. A shared
type would be the same length but would transpose fields, so each keeps its own
type and its byte-exact round trip:

- `HEADER_GC_SEPCIAL_EFFECT` (114) is `{ header; BYTE type; DWORD vid; }`. Its
  field **order** is the reverse of the 6-byte `{ header; DWORD vid; BYTE
  position; }` shape, so it cannot share that type. The legacy name contains a
  typo, `SEPCIAL`, which is preserved because the enumerator is the wire
  contract.
- `HEADER_GC_REFINE_ELEMENT` (228) is two `WORD`s then a `BYTE`.
- `HEADER_GC_CHANGE_SPEED` (18) is a `DWORD` then a `WORD`.
- `HEADER_GC_EVENT_KW_SCORE` (157) is three `WORD`s.

The wiring test `the_four_single_field_game_to_client_records_keep_their_own_field_order`
checks the exact bytes of each and then asserts that reading the last frame as
the first type fails on the header, so a future merge cannot pass by length
alone.

### 165.8 Four more records with no server producer

Whole-token searches over `server/server` return no producer for:

| byte | record | server hits |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 18 | `HEADER_GC_CHANGE_SPEED` | the enumerator at `packet.h:118` only |
| 73 | `HEADER_GC_SKILL_COOLTIME_END` | none (section 164) |
| 84 | `HEADER_GC_SAFEBOX_MONEY_CHANGE` | none |
| 112 | `HEADER_GC_CHANGE_SKILL_GROUP` | none (section 164) |
| 213 | `HEADER_GC_UNK_213` | none (section 164) |

The client registers and decodes all five. `HEADER_GC_SAFEBOX_MONEY_CHANGE` has
no server enumerator at all; the other four have an enumerator but no producer.
These are real client decode entries with real framing, so they are implemented,
but they are unreachable in the checked-in server and are better understood as
server reachability questions than as porting work. By contrast
`HEADER_GC_SKILL_COOLTIME_END` at byte 73 is also a header the client never
dispatches.

| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| client to game | 92 | 91 | 1 (dead) |
| game to game | 36 | 4 | 32 |

Game-to-client coverage is now 39 percent, up from 8 percent at the start of
